requirements.subject: ent:index-notation
requirements.canonical: In index notation within an assignment or mixed notation, an index SHALL NOT appear more than once.
requirements.original: In this notation each index shall not` appear more than once and shall conform to the range of indices allowed by the type definition.

requirements.subject: ent:index-notation
requirements.canonical: In index notation within an assignment or mixed notation, each index SHALL conform to the range of indices allowed by the type definition.
requirements.original: In this notation each index shall not` appear more than once and shall conform to the range of indices allowed by the type definition.

requirements.subject: ent:mixed-notation
requirements.canonical: In mixed notation, an element in value list notation SHALL NOT follow an element in assignment notation within the same immediate context.
requirements.original: It is allowed to mix the two value notations in the same (immediate) context only in such a way that elements in list notation do not follow elements in assignment notation.

requirements.subject: ent:recursive-type-definition
requirements.canonical: A TTCN-3 type definition MAY be recursive where applicable.
requirements.original: Where applicable TTCN-3 type definitions may be recursive.

requirements.subject: ent:recursive-type-definition
requirements.canonical: A recursive type definition SHALL be resolvable.
requirements.original: The user, however, shall ensure that all type recursion is resolvable and that no infinite recursion occurs.

ambiguity.issue: 'The user' is not a defined term; the test suite author / TTCN-3 module writer is meant.

requirements.subject: ent:recursive-type-definition
requirements.canonical: A recursive type definition SHALL NOT cause infinite recursion.
requirements.original: The user, however, shall ensure that all type recursion is resolvable and that no infinite recursion occurs.

requirements.subject: ent:field
requirements.canonical: In a record or set type, a field referencing its own enclosing type SHALL be optional.
requirements.original: In case of record and set types, to avoid infinite recursion, fields referencing to its own type, shall be optional.

ambiguity.issue: 'referencing its own type' can mean a field whose type is directly the enclosing type, or any field whose type (indirectly) contains the enclosing type, e.g. via a union; the direct reading was chosen.
readings: In a record or set type, a field whose type is the enclosing record or set type SHALL be optional.
In a record or set type, every field whose type directly or indirectly references the enclosing type SHALL be optional.

requirements.subject: ent:union-alternative
requirements.canonical: In a union type, at least one alternative SHALL NOT reference the union type itself.
requirements.original: In case of union types, to avoid infinite recursion, at least one of the alternatives shall not reference its own type.

requirements.subject: ent:record-type
requirements.canonical: A record type IS an ordered structured type.
requirements.original: TTCN-3 supports ordered structured types known as record.

requirements.subject: ent:record-field
requirements.canonical: A field of a record type MAY be of any TTCN-3 type.
requirements.original: The fields of a record type may be of any TTCN-3 type.

requirements.subject: ent:record-value
requirements.canonical: Each field value of a record value SHALL be compatible with the type of the corresponding record field.
requirements.original: The values of a record shall be compatible with the types of the record fields.

requirements.subject: ent:field-identifier
requirements.canonical: A field identifier of a record type IS local to that record type.
requirements.original: The field identifiers are local to the record and shall be unique within the record (but do not have to be globally unique).

requirements.subject: ent:field-identifier
requirements.canonical: A field identifier SHALL be unique within its record type.
requirements.original: The field identifiers are local to the record and shall be unique within the record (but do not have to be globally unique).

requirements.subject: ent:field-identifier
requirements.canonical: A field identifier of a record type NEED NOT be globally unique.
requirements.original: The field identifiers are local to the record and shall be unique within the record (but do not have to be globally unique).

requirements.subject: ent:record-type
requirements.canonical: A record type MAY be defined with no fields (empty record).
requirements.original: Records may be defined with no fields, i.e. as empty records.

requirements.subject: ent:record-value
requirements.canonical: A record value IS assigned on an individual field basis.
requirements.original: A record value is assigned on an individual field basis.

requirements.subject: ent:value-list-notation
requirements.canonical: In value list notation for a record value, the order of the field values SHALL be the same as the order of the fields in the record type definition.
requirements.original: The order of field values in the value list notation shall be the same as the order of fields in the related type definition.

requirements.subject: ent:assignment-notation
requirements.condition: the assignment notation is used for a record value
requirements.canonical: When the assignment notation is used for a record value, each field to be changed SHALL be identified explicitly.
requirements.original: When the assignment notation is used for record-s, fields wished to be changed shall be identified explicitly and a value, the not used symbol "-" or the omit keyword can be associated with them.

requirements.subject: ent:assignment-notation
requirements.canonical: In assignment notation for a record value, an explicitly identified field MAY be associated with a value, the not used symbol "-" or the `omit` keyword.
requirements.original: When the assignment notation is used for record-s, fields wished to be changed shall be identified explicitly and a value, the not used symbol "-" or the omit keyword can be associated with them.

requirements.subject: ent:omit-keyword
requirements.condition: assignment notation is used for a record value
requirements.canonical: In assignment notation, the `omit` keyword SHALL only be used for optional fields.
requirements.original: The `omit` keyword shall only be used for optional fields.

requirements.subject: ent:omit-keyword
requirements.canonical: An optional field assigned `omit` in assignment notation IS not present in the resulting value.
requirements.original: Its result is that the given field is not present in the given value.

requirements.subject: ent:mandatory-field
requirements.canonical: A mandatory field that is not explicitly referred to in the assignment notation, or is explicitly unspecified using the not used symbol "-", SHALL remain unchanged.
requirements.original: Mandatory fields, not explicitly referred to in the notation or explicitly unspecified using the not used symbol "-", shall remain unchanged.

requirements.subject: ent:assignment-notation
requirements.condition: partial value specified with assignment notation at initialization
requirements.canonical: When a partial value is specified using the assignment notation at initialization, only the fields to be assigned values SHALL be specified.
requirements.original: In particular, when specifying partial values (i.e. setting the value of only a subset of the fields) using the assignment notation, at initialization, only the fields to be assigned values shall be specified.

ambiguity.issue: 'only ... shall be specified' can be read as a relaxation (other fields need not be listed) or as a prohibition of listing other fields; the relaxation reading was chosen as it matches the surrounding text and examples.
readings: When a partial value is specified using the assignment notation at initialization, only the fields to be assigned values NEED be specified.
When a partial value is specified using the assignment notation at initialization, fields not assigned a value SHALL NOT be listed (e.g. with the not used symbol).

requirements.subject: ent:record-field
requirements.condition: the optional attribute is not "implicit omit"
requirements.canonical: At initialization with the assignment notation, a field not mentioned in the notation IS implicitly left uninitialized.
requirements.original: Fields not mentioned are implicitly left uninitialized.

requirements.subject: ent:record-field
requirements.canonical: When a previously initialized value is re-assigned using the assignment notation, a field skipped or given the not used symbol "-" IS left unchanged.
requirements.original: When re-assigning a previously initialized value, using the not used symbol or just skipping a field in an assignment notation, will cause that field to remain unchanged.

requirements.subject: ent:assignment-notation
requirements.canonical: A field SHALL NOT appear more than once in an assignment notation, also when a partial value is specified.
requirements.original: Even when specifying partial values each field shall not appear more than once.

requirements.subject: ent:omitted-field
requirements.canonical: An omitted optional field IS intentionally not present in the record or set value and IS considered initialized, unlike an uninitialized field.
requirements.original: Omitted optional fields are not present in the record or set value intentionally, i.e. the field is initialized and it does not prevent the whole record or set from being completely initialized.

requirements.subject: ent:omitted-field
requirements.canonical: An omitted optional field IS NOT an obstacle to the record or set value being completely initialized.
requirements.original: Omitted optional fields are not present in the record or set value intentionally, i.e. the field is initialized and it does not prevent the whole record or set from being completely initialized.

requirements.subject: ent:assignment-notation
requirements.condition: optional attribute is "explicit omit"
requirements.canonical: When the assignment notation is used in a scope where the optional attribute is implicitly or explicitly set to "explicit omit", optional and mandatory fields not directly referred to in the notation SHALL remain unchanged.
requirements.original: When the assignment notation is used in a scope, where the optional attribute is implicitly or explicitly set to "explicit omit", optional and mandatory fields, not directly referred to in the notation shall remain unchanged.

requirements.subject: ent:optional-field
requirements.condition: optional fields of variables are not assigned explicitly
requirements.canonical: An optional field of a variable that is not assigned explicitly IS uninitialized.
requirements.original: When optional fields of variables are not assigned explicitly, they are uninitialized (i.e. the optional attribute shall not have any effect on variables as described in clause 27.7 restriction a)).

requirements.subject: ent:optional-attribute
requirements.canonical: The optional attribute SHALL NOT have any effect on variables.
requirements.original: When optional fields of variables are not assigned explicitly, they are uninitialized (i.e. the optional attribute shall not have any effect on variables as described in clause 27.7 restriction a)).

requirements.subject: ent:optional-field
requirements.condition: optional attribute is "implicit omit"
requirements.canonical: When the assignment notation is used in a scope where the optional attribute is set to "implicit omit", optional fields not directly referred to in the notation SHALL implicitly be set to `omit`.
requirements.original: When the assignment notation is used in a scope, where the optional attribute is set to "implicit `omit",` optional fields, not directly referred to in the notation, shall implicitly be set to omit, while mandatory fields shall remain unchanged (see also clause 27.7).

requirements.subject: ent:mandatory-field
requirements.condition: optional attribute is "implicit omit"
requirements.canonical: When the assignment notation is used in a scope where the optional attribute is set to "implicit omit", mandatory fields not directly referred to in the notation SHALL remain unchanged.
requirements.original: When the assignment notation is used in a scope, where the optional attribute is set to "implicit `omit",` optional fields, not directly referred to in the notation, shall implicitly be set to omit, while mandatory fields shall remain unchanged (see also clause 27.7).

requirements.subject: ent:value-list-notation
requirements.canonical: In value list notation for a record value, every field listed SHALL be specified with a value, the not used symbol "-" or the `omit` keyword.
requirements.original: When using the value list notation, all fields listed in the notation shall be specified either with a value, the not used symbol "-" or the omit keyword.

requirements.subject: ent:omit-keyword
requirements.canonical: In value list notation, the `omit` keyword SHALL only be used for optional fields.
requirements.original: The omit keyword shall only be used for optional fields.

requirements.subject: ent:omit-keyword
requirements.canonical: An optional field given `omit` in value list notation IS not present in the resulting value.
requirements.original: Its result is that the given field is not present in the given value.

requirements.subject: ent:value-list-notation
requirements.canonical: In value list notation, the n-th list component (a value, "-" or `omit`) IS associated with the n-th field of the record type.
requirements.original: The first component of the list (a value, a "-" or omit) is associated with the first field, the second list component is associated with the second field, etc.

requirements.subject: ent:value-list-notation
requirements.canonical: A value list notation SHALL NOT contain an empty assignment (two commas immediately following each other or separated only by white space).
requirements.original: No empty assignment is allowed (i.e. two commas, the second immediately following the first or only with white space between them).

requirements.subject: ent:not-used-symbol
requirements.canonical: In value list notation, a field to be left unchanged that is followed by fields assigned a value or template explicitly SHALL be skipped by using the not used symbol "-".
requirements.original: Fields to be left unchanged, but followed by fields to which a value or template is assigned explicitly, shall be skipped by using the not used symbol "-".

requirements.subject: ent:value-list-notation
requirements.condition: optional attribute is "explicit omit"
requirements.canonical: When value list notation is used in a scope where the optional attribute is implicitly or explicitly set to "explicit omit", the remaining fields at the end of the type definition missing from the notation ARE left unchanged.
requirements.original: When using value list notation in a scope where the optional attribute is implicitly or explicitly set to "explicit omit", all remaining fields at the end of the type definition, missing from the value list notation, are left unchanged.

requirements.subject: ent:not-used-symbol
requirements.condition: optional attribute is "implicit omit"
requirements.canonical: When value list notation is used in a scope where the optional attribute is set to "implicit omit", an optional field to be omitted by the implicit mechanism that is followed by explicitly assigned fields SHALL be skipped by using the not used symbol "-".
requirements.original: When using value list notation in a scope where the optional attribute is set to "implicit omit", optional fields wished to be omitted by the implicit mechanism, but followed by fields to which a value or template is assigned explicitly, shall be skipped by using the not used symbol "-".

requirements.subject: ent:value-list-notation
requirements.condition: optional attribute is "implicit omit" and all trailing fields are optional
requirements.canonical: When all remaining fields at the end of the type definition are optional and are to be omitted by the implicit omit mechanism, the not used symbol "-" MAY be used for some or all of them, or they MAY be left out of the value list notation.
requirements.original: When all remaining fields at the end of the type definition are optional and they are wished to be omitted by the implicit mechanism, either the not used symbol "-" can be used for some or all of them or they can simply be left out from the notation.

requirements.subject: ent:optional-field
requirements.condition: optional attribute is "implicit omit"
requirements.canonical: When a record value is assigned from a referenced value in a scope where the optional attribute is set to "implicit omit", the uninitialized optional fields of the referenced value SHALL be set to `omit` in the new value.
requirements.original: When using direct assignment notation in a scope where the optional attribute is set to "implicit omit", the uninitialized optional fields in the referenced value, shall implicitly be set to omit after the assignment in the new value, while mandatory fields shall remain unchanged (see also clause 27.7).

ambiguity.issue: 'direct assignment notation' is not a defined term; it means assigning a reference to an existing value (e.g. c_x4 := c_x3).

requirements.subject: ent:mandatory-field
requirements.condition: optional attribute is "implicit omit"
requirements.canonical: When a record value is assigned from a referenced value in a scope where the optional attribute is set to "implicit omit", the mandatory fields SHALL remain unchanged.
requirements.original: When using direct assignment notation in a scope where the optional attribute is set to "implicit omit", the uninitialized optional fields in the referenced value, shall implicitly be set to omit after the assignment in the new value, while mandatory fields shall remain unchanged (see also clause 27.7).

ambiguity.issue: 'direct assignment notation' is not a defined term; it means assigning a reference to an existing value.

requirements.subject: ent:fuzzy-modifier
requirements.canonical: A field assignment in a record value or template MAY be prefixed by the `@fuzzy` modifier.
requirements.original: A field assignment in a record value or template can be prefixed by the @fuzzy modifier to declare that the right hand side of the assignment shall only be evaluated when used in a matching, receiving or sending operation, as a non-lazy or non-fuzzy operand to an expression, as a non-lazy or non-fuzzy actual parameter or on the right-hand-side of an assignment to a non-lazy or non-fuzzy variable, template variable or template.

requirements.subject: ent:fuzzy-modifier
requirements.canonical: The right hand side of a `@fuzzy` field assignment SHALL only be evaluated when used in a matching, receiving or sending operation, as a non-lazy or non-fuzzy operand of an expression, as a non-lazy or non-fuzzy actual parameter, or on the right hand side of an assignment to a non-lazy or non-fuzzy variable, template variable or template.
requirements.original: A field assignment in a record value or template can be prefixed by the @fuzzy modifier to declare that the right hand side of the assignment shall only be evaluated when used in a matching, receiving or sending operation, as a non-lazy or non-fuzzy operand to an expression, as a non-lazy or non-fuzzy actual parameter or on the right-hand-side of an assignment to a non-lazy or non-fuzzy variable, template variable or template.

requirements.subject: ent:dot-notation
requirements.canonical: A field of a record SHALL be referenced by the dot notation TypeIdOrExpression.ElementId.
requirements.original: Elements of a record shall be referenced by the dot notation TypeIdOrExpression.ElementId, where TypeIdOrExpression resolves to the name of a structured type or an expression of a structured type such as variable, formal parameter, module parameter, constant, template, or function invocation.

ambiguity.issue: 'elements' is used where record 'fields' is meant.

requirements.subject: ent:dot-notation
requirements.canonical: In a dot notation, TypeIdOrExpression SHALL resolve to the name of a structured type or to an expression of a structured type, such as a variable, formal parameter, module parameter, constant, template or function invocation.
requirements.original: Elements of a record shall be referenced by the dot notation TypeIdOrExpression.ElementId, where TypeIdOrExpression resolves to the name of a structured type or an expression of a structured type such as variable, formal parameter, module parameter, constant, template, or function invocation.

requirements.subject: ent:dot-notation
requirements.canonical: In a dot notation, ElementId SHALL resolve to the name of a field of the structured type.
requirements.original: ElementId shall resolve to the name of a field in the structured type.

requirements.subject: ent:record-field
requirements.canonical: A field of a record type definition SHALL NOT reference itself in its type (e.g. `MyType.field2 field2`).
requirements.original: Fields of record type definitions shall not reference themselves.

ambiguity.issue: 'reference themselves' may mean only a field type that references the same field via dot notation (as in the example) or any (also indirect) circular field-type reference; recursive record types via optional fields are allowed elsewhere. The direct reading matching the example was chosen.
readings: A field type of a record type definition SHALL NOT be a reference to that same field (e.g. `MyType.field2 field2`).
A field type of a record type definition SHALL NOT directly or indirectly depend on the field itself.

requirements.subject: ent:dot-notation
requirements.canonical: The type of a field of a record type or record subtype referenced by dot notation IS the set of values allowed by the constraints of the field declaration itself.
requirements.original: If a field in a record type or a subtype of a record type is referenced by the dot notation, the resulting type is the set of values allowed for that field imposed by the constraints of the field declaration itself (i.e. any constraints applied to the **record type itself are ignored).**

requirements.subject: ent:subtype-constraint
requirements.canonical: Subtype constraints applied to the record type itself ARE ignored when a field type is referenced by dot notation.
requirements.original: If a field in a record type or a subtype of a record type is referenced by the dot notation, the resulting type is the set of values allowed for that field imposed by the constraints of the field declaration itself (i.e. any constraints applied to the **record type itself are ignored).**

requirements.subject: ent:dot-notation
requirements.canonical: Referencing a subfield of an uninitialized or omitted record field or value on the right hand side of an assignment SHALL cause an error.
requirements.original: Referencing a subfield of an uninitialized or omitted record field or value on the right hand side of an assignment shall cause an error.

requirements.subject: ent:dot-notation
requirements.canonical: When a field of an uninitialized record value or field, or of an omitted field (also omitted at a higher level), is referenced on the left hand side of an assignment, the reference SHALL recursively be expanded up to and including the depth of the referenced subfield.
requirements.original: When referencing a field of an uninitialized record value or field or omitted field (including omitting a field at a higher level of the embedding hierarchy) on the left hand side of an assignment, the reference shall recursively be expanded up to and including the depth of the referenced subfield as follows:

requirements.subject: ent:record-field
requirements.canonical: When a record value or field is expanded, the subfield referenced in the dot notation SHALL be set to present.
requirements.original: a) When expanding a value or value field of record type, the subfield referenced in the dot notation shall be set to present and all unreferenced mandatory subfields shall be left uninitialized; when the assignment is used in a scope where the optional attribute is equal to "explicit omit", all unreferenced optional subfields shall be left undefined.

requirements.subject: ent:mandatory-field
requirements.canonical: When a record value or field is expanded, all unreferenced mandatory subfields SHALL be left uninitialized.
requirements.original: a) When expanding a value or value field of record type, the subfield referenced in the dot notation shall be set to present and all unreferenced mandatory subfields shall be left uninitialized; when the assignment is used in a scope where the optional attribute is equal to "explicit omit", all unreferenced optional subfields shall be left undefined.

requirements.subject: ent:optional-field
requirements.condition: optional attribute is "explicit omit"
requirements.canonical: When a record value or field is expanded in a scope where the optional attribute is "explicit omit", all unreferenced optional subfields SHALL be left uninitialized.
requirements.original: a) When expanding a value or value field of record type, the subfield referenced in the dot notation shall be set to present and all unreferenced mandatory subfields shall be left uninitialized; when the assignment is used in a scope where the optional attribute is equal to "explicit omit", all unreferenced optional subfields shall be left undefined.

ambiguity.issue: 'undefined' is used where 'uninitialized' is meant.

requirements.subject: ent:optional-field
requirements.condition: optional attribute is "implicit omit"
requirements.canonical: When a record value or field is expanded in a scope where the optional attribute is "implicit omit", all unreferenced optional subfields SHALL be set to `omit`.
requirements.original: When the assignment is used in a scope where the optional attribute is equal to "implicit omit", all unreferenced optional subfields shall be set to omit.

requirements.subject: ent:dot-notation
requirements.canonical: Expansion of record of, set of and array values SHALL follow clause 6.2.7, expansion of union values SHALL follow clause 6.2.5.1, and expansion of set values SHALL follow clause 6.2.2.1.
requirements.original: b) Expansion of record of/set of/array, union and set values and intermediate fields shall follow the rules of item a) in clauses 6.2.7 and 6.2.5.1 and clause 6.2.2.1 correspondingly.

ambiguity.issue: 'item a) in clauses ... correspondingly' is unclear: clause 6.2.2.1 has no item a) and refers back to 6.2.1.1; it is unclear whether one rule applies to all three type groups or each group maps to one clause. The pairwise mapping was chosen.
readings: Expansion of record of/set of/array values SHALL follow 6.2.7, union values 6.2.5.1, and set values 6.2.2.1 (pairwise).
Expansion of all these values SHALL follow item a) of each of the clauses 6.2.7, 6.2.5.1 and 6.2.2.1.

requirements.subject: ent:dot-notation
requirements.canonical: At the end of the expansion, the value on the right hand side of the assignment SHALL be assigned to the referenced subfield.
requirements.original: At the end of the expansion, the value at the right hand side of the assignment shall be assigned to the referenced subfield.

requirements.subject: ent:optional-keyword
requirements.canonical: An optional field of a record type SHALL be specified using the `optional` keyword.
requirements.original: Optional elements in a record shall be specified using the optional keyword.

ambiguity.issue: 'elements' is used where record 'fields' is meant.

requirements.subject: ent:omit-keyword
requirements.canonical: An optional field SHALL be omitted using the `omit` keyword.
requirements.original: Optional fields shall be omitted using the omit symbol.

ambiguity.issue: 'omit symbol' is used where the `omit` keyword is meant.

requirements.subject: ent:nested-type-definition
requirements.canonical: A type of a record field MAY be defined nested within the record type definition.
requirements.original: TTCN-3 supports the definition of types for record fields nested within the record definition.

requirements.subject: ent:nested-type-definition
requirements.canonical: A nested type definition of a record field MAY define a new structured type (record, set, enumerated, set of, record of, union or map).
requirements.original: Both the definition of new structured types (record, set, enumerated, set `of, record` `of, union and map) and the specification of` subtype constraints are possible.

requirements.subject: ent:nested-type-definition
requirements.canonical: A nested type definition of a record field MAY specify subtype constraints.
requirements.original: Both the definition of new structured types (record, set, enumerated, set `of, record` `of, union and map) and the specification of` subtype constraints are possible.

requirements.subject: ent:embedded-field
requirements.canonical: A field defined with a type reference but no explicit field name IS an embedded field.
requirements.original: A field defined with a type reference but no explicit field name is called an embedded field.

requirements.subject: ent:embedded-field
requirements.canonical: The unqualified type name of an embedded field IS its field name.
requirements.original: The unqualified type name acts as the field name.

requirements.subject: ent:promoted-field
requirements.canonical: A field of an embedded field whose name has no conflicts with other field names IS a promoted field.
requirements.original: A field of an embedded field is called promoted if its name has no conflicts with other field names.

ambiguity.issue: It is not stated which field names are considered for conflicts (fields of the enclosing record only, or also fields of other embedded fields). The example (z conflicts with Pixel.z) supports the enclosing-record reading, chosen here.
readings: A field of an embedded field IS a promoted field if its name differs from all field names of the enclosing record.
A field of an embedded field IS a promoted field if its name differs from all field names of the enclosing record and of all other embedded fields.

requirements.subject: ent:promoted-field
requirements.canonical: A promoted field IS referenced like an ordinary field of the record.
requirements.original: Promoted fields act like ordinary fields of a record

requirements.subject: ent:promoted-field
requirements.canonical: A promoted field SHALL NOT be used as a field name in an assignment notation.
requirements.original: except that they shall not be used as field names for assignment notations.

requirements.subject: ent:set-type
requirements.canonical: A set type IS an unordered structured type.
requirements.original: TTCN-3 supports unordered structured types known as set.

requirements.subject: ent:set-type
requirements.canonical: The ordering of the fields of a set type IS NOT significant; otherwise set types and values follow the rules of record types.
requirements.original: Set types and values are similar to records except that the ordering of the set fields is not significant.

ambiguity.issue: 'similar to records' does not say whether all record rules apply to sets; the reading that all record rules apply except ordering was chosen.
readings: Set types and values follow all rules of record types except that field ordering IS NOT significant.
Set types and values only resemble record types; only the stated set-specific rules apply.

requirements.subject: ent:field-identifier
requirements.canonical: A field identifier of a set type IS local to that set type.
requirements.original: The field identifiers are local to the set and shall be unique within the set (but do not have to be globally unique).

requirements.subject: ent:field-identifier
requirements.canonical: A field identifier SHALL be unique within its set type.
requirements.original: The field identifiers are local to the set and shall be unique within the set (but do not have to be globally unique).

requirements.subject: ent:field-identifier
requirements.canonical: A field identifier of a set type NEED NOT be globally unique.
requirements.original: The field identifiers are local to the set and shall be unique within the set (but do not have to be globally unique).

requirements.subject: ent:value-list-notation
requirements.canonical: When value list notation is used for a set value, the values ARE assigned to the fields in the sequential order of the fields in the set type definition.
requirements.original: NOTE: When the value list notation is used for values of set types, the values are assigned to the fields in the sequential order of the fields in the type definition.

requirements.subject: ent:dot-notation
requirements.canonical: A field of a set SHALL be referenced by the dot notation.
requirements.original: Elements of a set shall be referenced by the dot notation (see clause 6.2.1.1).

ambiguity.issue: 'elements' is used where set 'fields' is meant.

requirements.subject: ent:set-field
requirements.canonical: A field of a set type definition SHALL NOT reference itself.
requirements.original: Elements of set type definitions shall not reference themselves.

ambiguity.issue: 'elements' is used where set 'fields' is meant.

requirements.subject: ent:set-field
requirements.canonical: The rules of clause 6.2.1.1 for referencing field types of record types SHALL apply to referencing field types of set types.
requirements.original: For referencing field types of set types, the same rules apply as in clause 6.2.1.1 for fields of **record types.**

requirements.subject: ent:optional-keyword
requirements.canonical: An optional field of a set type SHALL be specified using the `optional` keyword.
requirements.original: Optional elements in a set shall be specified using the optional keyword.

ambiguity.issue: 'elements' is used where set 'fields' is meant.

requirements.subject: ent:nested-type-definition
requirements.canonical: A type of a set field MAY be defined nested within the set type definition, as for record types.
requirements.original: TTCN-3 supports the definition of types for set fields nested within the set definition, similar to the mechanism for record types described in clause 6.2.1.3.

requirements.subject: ent:embedded-field
requirements.canonical: Embedded fields in a set type definition follow the same rules as embedded fields in record types.
requirements.original: Embedded Fields with the set definition are similar to the mechanism for record types described in clause 6.2.1.4.

requirements.subject: ent:ttcn3-tool
requirements.canonical: A TTCN-3 tool SHALL support the specification of record of types and set of types, whose elements are all of the same type.
requirements.original: TTCN-3 supports the specification of records and sets whose elements are all of the same type.

requirements.subject: ent:record-of-type
requirements.canonical: A record of type IS a record whose elements are all of the same type.
requirements.original: TTCN-3 supports the specification of records and sets whose elements are all of the same type.

requirements.subject: ent:set-of-type
requirements.canonical: A set of type IS a set whose elements are all of the same type.
requirements.original: TTCN-3 supports the specification of records and sets whose elements are all of the same type.

requirements.subject: ent:record-of-type
requirements.canonical: A record of type and a set of type ARE denoted using the keyword `of`.
requirements.original: These are denoted using the keyword of.

requirements.subject: ent:element
requirements.canonical: An element of a record of type or set of type IS NOT associated with an element identifier.
requirements.original: These records and sets do not have element identifiers and can be considered similar to an ordered array and an unordered collection respectively.

requirements.subject: ent:record-of-type
requirements.canonical: A record of type IS similar to an ordered array.
requirements.original: These records and sets do not have element identifiers and can be considered similar to an ordered array and an unordered collection respectively.

requirements.subject: ent:set-of-type
requirements.canonical: A set of type IS similar to an unordered collection.
requirements.original: These records and sets do not have element identifiers and can be considered similar to an ordered array and an unordered collection respectively.

requirements.subject: ent:assignment-notation
requirements.canonical: When the assignment notation is used for a record of or set of value, the elements to be changed ARE identified explicitly.
requirements.original: When the assignment notation is used for record of-s and set `of-s, elements wished to be changed are identified` explicitly and either a value or the not used symbol "-" can be assigned to them.

requirements.subject: ent:assignment-notation
requirements.canonical: In an assignment notation for a record of or set of value, either a value or the not used symbol "-" MAY be assigned to an explicitly identified element.
requirements.original: When the assignment notation is used for record of-s and set `of-s, elements wished to be changed are identified` explicitly and either a value or the not used symbol "-" can be assigned to them.

requirements.subject: ent:element
requirements.condition: the assignment notation is used for a record of or set of value
requirements.canonical: When the assignment notation is used for a record of or set of value, an element not referred to in the notation SHALL remain unchanged.
requirements.original: Other elements, not referred to in the notation, shall remain unchanged.

requirements.subject: ent:assignment-notation
requirements.condition: a partial value is specified using the assignment notation
requirements.canonical: When a partial record of or set of value is specified using the assignment notation, only the elements to be assigned values SHALL be specified.
requirements.original: In particular, when specifying partial values (i.e. setting the value of only a subset of the fields) using the assignment notation, for example, at initialization, only the elements to be assigned values shall be specified: elements not mentioned are implicitly left uninitialized.

ambiguity.issue: 'fields' is used for record of/set of values, which have elements, not fields.

requirements.subject: ent:element
requirements.canonical: When a partial record of or set of value is specified using the assignment notation, an element not mentioned IS implicitly left uninitialized.
requirements.original: In particular, when specifying partial values (i.e. setting the value of only a subset of the fields) using the assignment notation, for example, at initialization, only the elements to be assigned values shall be specified: elements not mentioned are implicitly left uninitialized.

requirements.subject: ent:not-used-symbol
requirements.canonical: An element of a record of or set of value MAY be left explicitly unspecified in an assignment notation using the not used symbol "-".
requirements.original: It is also possible to leave fields explicitly unspecified using the not used symbol "-".

ambiguity.issue: 'fields' is used for record of/set of values, which have elements, not fields.

requirements.subject: ent:element
requirements.condition: a previously initialized value is re-assigned
requirements.canonical: When a previously initialized record of or set of value is re-assigned with an assignment notation, an element that is skipped or assigned the not used symbol "-" SHALL remain unchanged.
requirements.original: When re-assigning a previously initialized value, using the not used symbol or just skipping a field or element in an assignment notation, will cause that field or element to remain unchanged.

requirements.subject: ent:value-list-notation
requirements.canonical: In a value list notation for a record of or set of value, every element position up to the last list member SHALL be specified either with a value or the not used symbol "-".
requirements.original: When using the value list notation, all elements in the structure shall be specified either with a value or the not used symbol "-".

ambiguity.issue: 'all elements in the structure' is unclear for record of/set of, whose length is determined by the list; s017 states that trailing elements without list member become uninitialized, so reading 1 was chosen.
readings: In a value list notation for a record of or set of value, every element position up to the last list member SHALL be specified either with a value or the not used symbol "-".
In a value list notation for a record of or set of value, all existing elements of the value SHALL be specified either with a value or the not used symbol "-".

requirements.subject: ent:value-list-notation
requirements.canonical: In a value list notation, the n-th list member IS assigned to the n-th element of the record of or set of value.
requirements.original: The first member of the list is assigned to the first element, the second list member is assigned to the second element, etc. No empty assignment is allowed (e.g. two commas, the second immediately following the first or only with white space between them).

requirements.subject: ent:value-list-notation
requirements.canonical: A value list notation SHALL NOT contain an empty assignment (two commas with nothing or only white space between them).
requirements.original: The first member of the list is assigned to the first element, the second list member is assigned to the second element, etc. No empty assignment is allowed (e.g. two commas, the second immediately following the first or only with white space between them).

requirements.subject: ent:not-used-symbol
requirements.canonical: An element to be left out of a value list notation assignment SHALL be explicitly skipped in the list by the not used symbol "-".
requirements.original: Elements to be left out of the assignment shall be explicitly skipped in the list by use of the not-used-symbol "-".

requirements.subject: ent:element
requirements.canonical: An already initialized element of a record of or set of value that has no corresponding list member at the end of a value list notation IS made uninitialized by the assignment.
requirements.original: Already initialized elements left without a corresponding list member in a value list notation (i.e. at the end of a list) are becoming uninitialized.

ambiguity.issue: 'becoming uninitialized' can mean the element stays present with an undefined value, or the element is removed so the length shrinks; example 3 ({0,1,2,3,4} := {0,1,-,2} gives a 4-element value) supports removal, but the text says 'uninitialized'. The text wording was kept.
readings: A trailing initialized element without a corresponding list member IS kept as an uninitialized element and the length of the value IS unchanged.
A trailing initialized element without a corresponding list member IS removed and the length of the value IS reduced to the number of list members.

requirements.subject: ent:empty-value-list
requirements.canonical: Assigning the empty value list notation "{}" to a record of or set of value with initialized elements makes the value empty.
requirements.original: In this way, a value with initialized elements can be made empty by using the empty value list notation ("{}").

requirements.subject: ent:index-notation
requirements.canonical: The index notation MAY be used on both the right hand side and the left hand side of an assignment.
requirements.original: Index notation can be used on both the right-hand side and left-hand side of assignments.

requirements.subject: ent:index-notation
requirements.canonical: An index notation on the right hand side of an assignment refers to the value of the identified element of a record of or set of value.
requirements.original: The index notation, when used on the right-hand side, refers to the value of the identified element of a record of or a set of.

requirements.subject: ent:index-notation
requirements.condition: the index notation is used on the left hand side of an assignment
requirements.canonical: When the index notation is used on the left hand side of an assignment, only the value of the identified single element SHALL be changed and the values of the other elements SHALL remain unchanged.
requirements.original: When it is used at the left-hand side, only the value of the identified single element is changed, values assigned to other elements already remain unchanged.

requirements.subject: ent:index-notation
requirements.canonical: The index of the first element of a record of or set of value SHALL be zero.
requirements.original: The index of the first element shall be zero and the index value shall not exceed the limitation placed by length subtyping.

requirements.subject: ent:index-notation
requirements.canonical: The index value in an index notation SHALL NOT exceed the limitation placed by length subtyping of the record of or set of type.
requirements.original: The index of the first element shall be zero and the index value shall not exceed the limitation placed by length subtyping.

ambiguity.issue: 'shall not exceed the limitation' does not say whether the index is compared with the upper length bound or with the upper bound minus one (indices start at zero). Reading 1 (index < upper bound) was chosen as consistent with zero-based indexing.
readings: The index value SHALL be less than the upper length bound of the record of or set of type.
The index value SHALL be less than or equal to the upper length bound of the record of or set of type.

requirements.subject: ent:index-notation
requirements.condition: the referenced element is uninitialized
requirements.canonical: If the element indicated by an index notation on the right hand side of an assignment is uninitialized, this SHALL cause a semantic or runtime error.
requirements.original: If the value of the element indicated by the index at the right-hand of an assignment is undefined (uninitialized), this shall cause a semantic or runtime error.

ambiguity.issue: 'right-hand of an assignment' is used instead of the glossary term 'right hand side (of assignment)'.

requirements.subject: ent:index-notation
requirements.canonical: Referencing an element of an uninitialized or omitted record of or set of field or value on the right hand side of an assignment SHALL cause an error.
requirements.original: Referencing an identified element of an uninitialized or omitted record of or set of field or value on the right-hand side of an assignment shall cause an error.

requirements.subject: ent:index-notation
requirements.condition: the index refers to a non-existent element
requirements.canonical: If an index notation on the left hand side of an assignment refers to a non-existent element, the value at the right hand side IS assigned to that element.
requirements.original: If an indexing operator at the left-hand side of an assignment refers to a non-existent element, the value at the right-hand side is assigned to the element and all elements with an index smaller than the actual index and without assigned value are created with an uninitialized value.

requirements.subject: ent:element
requirements.condition: the index refers to a non-existent element
requirements.canonical: If an index notation on the left hand side of an assignment refers to a non-existent element, every element with a smaller index and without an assigned value IS created with an uninitialized value.
requirements.original: If an indexing operator at the left-hand side of an assignment refers to a non-existent element, the value at the right-hand side is assigned to the element and all elements with an index smaller than the actual index and without assigned value are created with an uninitialized value.

requirements.subject: ent:index-notation
requirements.condition: the record of or set of type is nested
requirements.canonical: For nested record of or set of types, an array or record of integer restricted to a single size MAY be used as a short-hand notation for a nested index notation.
requirements.original: For nested record of or set of types, an array or record of integer restricted to a single size can be used as a short-hand notation for a nested index notation.

requirements.subject: ent:reference-expansion
requirements.condition: the referenced element belongs to an uninitialized or omitted record of/set of value or field
requirements.canonical: When an element of an uninitialized record of or set of value or field or of an omitted field is referenced on the left hand side of an assignment, the reference SHALL be recursively expanded up to and including the depth of the referenced element.
requirements.original: When referencing an element of an uninitialized record of or set of value or field or omitted field (including omitting a field at a higher level of the embedding hierarchy) on the left-hand side of an assignment, the reference shall recursively be expanded up to and including the depth of the referenced element as follows:

requirements.subject: ent:reference-expansion
requirements.canonical: When expanding a record of or set of value or value field, the element referenced by the index notation SHALL be set to present.
requirements.original: a) When expanding a value or value field of record of or set of type, the element referenced by the index notation shall be set to present and all elements with a smaller index shall be created with an uninitialized value.

requirements.subject: ent:reference-expansion
requirements.canonical: When expanding a record of or set of value or value field, all elements with a smaller index than the referenced element SHALL be created with an uninitialized value.
requirements.original: a) When expanding a value or value field of record of or set of type, the element referenced by the index notation shall be set to present and all elements with a smaller index shall be created with an uninitialized value.

requirements.subject: ent:reference-expansion
requirements.canonical: Expansion of record, union and set values and intermediate fields SHALL follow item a) of clauses 6.2.1.1, 6.2.5.1 and 6.2.2.1 respectively.
requirements.original: b) Expansion of record, union and set values and intermediate fields shall follow the rules of item a) in clauses 6.2.1.1 and 6.2.5.1 and clause 6.2.2.1 correspondingly.

requirements.subject: ent:reference-expansion
requirements.canonical: At the end of the expansion, the value at the right hand side of the assignment SHALL be assigned to the referenced element.
requirements.original: c) At the end of the expansion, the value at the right-hand side of the assignment shall be assigned to the referenced element.

requirements.subject: ent:uninitialized-element
requirements.canonical: A record of or set of value SHALL NOT contain uninitialized elements except in transient states while the value remains invisible.
requirements.original: Uninitialized elements are permitted only in transient states (while the value remains invisible).

ambiguity.issue: 'transient states' and 'invisible' are not defined; it is unclear which uses of the value make it visible. Reading 1 was chosen because s032 names sending as the error case.
readings: Uninitialized elements cause an error only when the value becomes externally visible, e.g. when it is sent.
Any use of a record of or set of value containing uninitialized elements other than assignment to its elements (e.g. comparison, passing as a parameter) causes an error.

requirements.subject: ent:send-operation
requirements.canonical: Sending a record of or set of value with uninitialized elements SHALL cause an error.
requirements.original: Sending a record `of` or set of value with uninitialized elements shall cause an error.

requirements.subject: ent:assignment-notation
requirements.canonical: An assignment notation and an index notation used to change elements of a record of or set of value have a similar effect.
requirements.original: NOTE 2: When using on the right-hand side of an assignment for record of-s or set `of-s, the assignment` notation and the indexed notation have similar effect, with the exception that the assignment notation is able to address multiple elements in one notation, while the index notation is able to address a single element only.

ambiguity.issue: The note says both notations are used 'on the right-hand side of an assignment', but example 3 shows the equivalent index notation on the left hand side (v_ix[3] := ...). Reading 1 was chosen per example 3.
readings: An assignment notation on the right hand side and an index notation on the left hand side of an assignment have a similar effect.
An assignment notation and an index notation both used on the right hand side of an assignment have a similar effect.

requirements.subject: ent:assignment-notation
requirements.canonical: An assignment notation CAN address multiple elements in one notation, while an index notation CAN address a single element only.
requirements.original: NOTE 2: When using on the right-hand side of an assignment for record of-s or set `of-s, the assignment` notation and the indexed notation have similar effect, with the exception that the assignment notation is able to address multiple elements in one notation, while the index notation is able to address a single element only.

requirements.subject: ent:index-notation
requirements.canonical: The index notation CAN be used to copy record of values element by element in a for loop.
requirements.original: NOTE 3: The index notation makes it possible e.g. to copy record of values element by element in a for loop.

requirements.subject: ent:record-of-type
requirements.canonical: Embedded record of and set of types result in a data structure similar to multidimensional arrays.
requirements.original: Embedded record of and set of types will result in a data structure similar to multidimensional arrays (see clause 15.8.2).

requirements.subject: ent:nested-type-definition
requirements.canonical: The element type of a record of or set of type definition MAY be specified by a nested type definition.
requirements.original: TTCN-3 supports the definition of the aggregated type nested with the record `of or set` `of definition.

ambiguity.issue: 'aggregated type' is used instead of 'structured type'.

requirements.subject: ent:nested-type-definition
requirements.canonical: A nested type definition within a record of or set of type definition MAY define a new record, set, enumerated, set of or record of type.
requirements.original: Both the` definition of new structured types (record, set, enumerated, set `of and record` `of) and the specification of` subtype constraints are possible.

ambiguity.issue: The parenthesised list omits union types; it is unclear whether the list is exhaustive. Reading 1 (the list is exhaustive as written) was chosen.
readings: A nested type definition within a record of or set of type definition MAY define only a record, set, enumerated, set of or record of type.
A nested type definition within a record of or set of type definition MAY define any structured type (including union), the list being illustrative.

requirements.subject: ent:subtype-constraint
requirements.canonical: A nested type definition within a record of or set of type definition MAY specify subtype constraints.
requirements.original: Both the` definition of new structured types (record, set, enumerated, set `of and record` `of) and the specification of` subtype constraints are possible.

requirements.subject: ent:inner-type-reference
requirements.canonical: The inner type of a record of or set of type MAY be referenced by using the index notation with a dash.
requirements.original: It is also allowed to reference the inner type of record of and set of types by using the index notation but with a dash.

requirements.subject: ent:inner-type-reference
requirements.canonical: The notation TypeId[-], where TypeId resolves to the name of a record of or set of type, references the inner type of TypeId.
requirements.original: The notation TypeId[-], where TypeId resolves to the name of a record of or set of type, references the inner type of TypeId.

requirements.subject: ent:inner-type-reference
requirements.condition: the type definition restricts the element type
requirements.canonical: If the type definition of a record of or set of type restricts its element type, the inner type reference yields a type which contains all values of the constrained element type.
requirements.original: If the type definition restricts the element type of the record of or set of type, referencing the inner type of that type yields a type which contains all values from the constrained type.

ambiguity.issue: 'contains all values from the constrained type' does not state whether the yielded type is exactly the constrained element type or may be wider. Example (ConstrainedRecordOfInt[-]) shows the element constraint is kept, so reading 1 was chosen.
readings: The inner type reference yields exactly the constrained element type (the element subtype constraint is kept).
The inner type reference yields a type that includes all values of the constrained element type, possibly the unconstrained element type.

requirements.subject: ent:inner-type-reference
requirements.canonical: A length restriction of the outer record of type IS NOT part of the inner type yielded by an inner type reference.

requirements.subject: ent:ttcn3-tool
requirements.canonical: A TTCN-3 tool SHALL support enumerated types.
requirements.original: TTCN-3 supports enumerated types.

requirements.subject: ent:enumerated-type
requirements.canonical: An enumerated type IS a type that takes only values from a distinct named set of values.
requirements.original: Enumerated types are used to model types that take only a distinct named set of values.

requirements.subject: ent:enumerated-value
requirements.canonical: A distinct named value of an enumerated type IS called an enumerated value.
requirements.original: Such distinct values are called enumerated values.

requirements.subject: ent:enumerated-value
requirements.canonical: An enumerated value SHALL have an identifier.
requirements.original: Each enumerated value shall have an identifier and referencing the values shall only use these identifiers.

requirements.subject: ent:enumerated-value
requirements.canonical: A reference to an enumerated value SHALL only use the identifier of the enumerated value.
requirements.original: Each enumerated value shall have an identifier and referencing the values shall only use these identifiers.

requirements.subject: ent:enumerated-value
requirements.canonical: A reference to an enumerated value IS either in unqualified or in qualified form.
requirements.original: References to enumerated values can occur in two forms: unqualified and qualified.

requirements.subject: ent:unqualified-name
requirements.canonical: The unqualified form of an enumerated value reference consists only of the identifier of the enumerated value.
requirements.original: The unqualified form uses only the identifier of the enumerated value.

requirements.subject: ent:qualified-name
requirements.canonical: The qualified form of an enumerated value reference consists of the enumerated type reference, followed by a dot and the enumerated value identifier.
requirements.original: The qualified form consists of the enumerated type reference, followed by a dot and the enumerated value identifier.

requirements.subject: ent:identifier
requirements.canonical: The identifiers of the enumerated values SHALL be unique within the enumerated type.
requirements.original: The identifiers of enumerated values shall be unique within the enumerated type (but do not have to be globally unique) and are consequently visible in the context of the given type only.

requirements.subject: ent:identifier
requirements.canonical: The identifier of an enumerated value NEED NOT be globally unique.
requirements.original: The identifiers of enumerated values shall be unique within the enumerated type (but do not have to be globally unique) and are consequently visible in the context of the given type only.

requirements.subject: ent:identifier
requirements.canonical: The identifier of an enumerated value IS visible in the context of its enumerated type only.
requirements.original: The identifiers of enumerated values shall be unique within the enumerated type (but do not have to be globally unique) and are consequently visible in the context of the given type only.

requirements.subject: ent:enumerated-type
requirements.canonical: For any instantiation or value reference of an enumerated type, the enumerated type SHALL be implicitly or explicitly identified.
requirements.original: This means that for any instantiation or value reference of an enumerated type, the given type shall be implicitly or explicitly identified.

requirements.subject: ent:type-context
requirements.canonical: If an enumerated type is the type of an element or field of a structured type, the enumerated type IS implicitly referenced via the given element or field at value assignment and instantiation.
requirements.original: NOTE 1: For example, if the enumerated type is an element or field of a user defined structured type, the enumerated type is implicitly referenced via the given element/field (i.e. by the identifier of the field or the position of the value in a value list notation) at value assignment, instantiation, etc. Another example is passing an enumerated value as actual parameter, in which case the type of the corresponding formal parameter establishes the type context needed to make the enumeration value visible.

requirements.subject: ent:formal-parameter
requirements.canonical: When an enumerated value is passed as an actual parameter, the type of the corresponding formal parameter establishes the type context that makes the enumerated value visible.
requirements.original: NOTE 1: For example, if the enumerated type is an element or field of a user defined structured type, the enumerated type is implicitly referenced via the given element/field (i.e. by the identifier of the field or the position of the value in a value list notation) at value assignment, instantiation, etc. Another example is passing an enumerated value as actual parameter, in which case the type of the corresponding formal parameter establishes the type context needed to make the enumeration value visible.

ambiguity.issue: 'enumeration value' is used instead of 'enumerated value'.

requirements.subject: ent:comparison-operator
requirements.canonical: For a comparison operator, if the type of one of the operands is uniquely identified, it IS used as the type context for the other operand.
requirements.original: The third example is the comparison operators: if the type of one of the operands is uniquely identified, it is used as a type context for the other operand (see example 2 below).

requirements.subject: ent:match-operation
requirements.canonical: For the match operation, if the type of the value parameter is not identified, the type of the template parameter establishes the type context.
requirements.original: The fourth example is the match operation, where the type of the template parameter establishes the type context for the operation, if the type of the value parameter is not identified (see example 2 in clause 15.8.2).

requirements.subject: ent:identifier
requirements.canonical: Within the same module, the identifier of an enumerated value SHALL only be reused within other structured type definitions.
requirements.original: The identifiers of enumerated values, within the same module, shall only be reused within other structured type definitions and shall not be used for identifiers of local or global visibility at the same or a lower level of the same branch of the scope hierarchy (see scope hierarchy in clause 5.2).

requirements.subject: ent:identifier
requirements.canonical: Within the same module, the identifier of an enumerated value SHALL NOT be used for an identifier of local or global visibility at the same or a lower level of the same branch of the scope hierarchy.
requirements.original: The identifiers of enumerated values, within the same module, shall only be reused within other structured type definitions and shall not be used for identifiers of local or global visibility at the same or a lower level of the same branch of the scope hierarchy (see scope hierarchy in clause 5.2).

ambiguity.issue: Example 1 declares 'type integer Monday' at module level next to an enumerated type containing Monday and states it does not clash, which contradicts a literal reading of the prohibition (the module level is the same level as the enumerated type definition). Reading 1 (literal text) was chosen.
readings: A definition at the same or lower scope level as the enumerated type definition SHALL NOT reuse an enumerated value identifier (so 'type integer Monday' at module level is an error).

Because enumerated value identifiers are local to their type, only definitions inside the scope of that type context are restricted, and a module-level definition such as 'type integer Monday' is allowed.

requirements.subject: ent:enumerated-value
requirements.canonical: An enumerated value MAY have a user-assigned integer expression or a non-empty list of integer literal values or ranges of integer literal values, given in parentheses after the name of the enumerated value.
requirements.original: Each enumerated value may optionally have a user-assigned integer expression or non-empty list of integer literal values or ranges of integer literal values, which is defined after the name of the enumerated value in parenthesis.

requirements.subject: ent:associated-integer-value
requirements.canonical: A user-assigned integer expression of an enumerated value SHALL be statically bound and known at compilation time.
requirements.original: Each user assigned expression shall be statically bound, known in compilation time, and evaluate to an integer value.

requirements.subject: ent:associated-integer-value
requirements.canonical: A user-assigned integer expression of an enumerated value SHALL evaluate to an integer value.
requirements.original: Each user assigned expression shall be statically bound, known in compilation time, and evaluate to an integer value.

requirements.subject: ent:associated-integer-value
requirements.canonical: Each user-assigned integer value SHALL be distinct within a single enumerated type.
requirements.original: Each user-assigned integer value shall be distinct within a single enumerated type, all ranges of all the values lists shall be disjoint and shall not include any of the used single integer values.

requirements.subject: ent:integer-value-list
requirements.canonical: All ranges of all integer value lists of an enumerated type SHALL be disjoint.
requirements.original: Each user-assigned integer value shall be distinct within a single enumerated type, all ranges of all the values lists shall be disjoint and shall not include any of the used single integer values.

requirements.subject: ent:integer-value-list
requirements.canonical: A range in an integer value list of an enumerated type SHALL NOT include any of the single integer values used in that enumerated type.
requirements.original: Each user-assigned integer value shall be distinct within a single enumerated type, all ranges of all the values lists shall be disjoint and shall not include any of the used single integer values.

requirements.subject: ent:associated-integer-value
requirements.canonical: An enumerated value without an assigned integer value IS associated with an integer number in the textual order of the enumerated values, starting at the left-hand side with zero, in steps of 1, skipping any number occupied by an enumerated value with a manually assigned value or value list.
requirements.original: For each enumerated value without an assigned integer value, the system successively associates an integer number in the textual order of the enumerated values, starting at the left-hand side, beginning with zero, by step 1 and skipping any number occupied by any of the enumerated values with a manually assigned value or value list.

requirements.subject: ent:associated-integer-value
requirements.canonical: The integer values associated with enumerated values ARE used to evaluate relational operators on enumerated values.
requirements.original: These values are only used by the system to allow the use of relational operators.

requirements.subject: ent:enumerated-value
requirements.canonical: An enumerated value with an associated integer value list SHALL only be used as a value together with a specific integer value in parentheses after its name.
requirements.original: Enumerated names with an associated value list shall only be used as values together with a specific integer value, which shall be one from the associated list, in parenthesis after the name.

ambiguity.issue: 'enumerated names' is used instead of 'enumerated values' (or their identifiers).

requirements.subject: ent:associated-integer-value
requirements.canonical: The integer value given in parentheses after an enumerated value with an associated integer value list SHALL be one of the values of that list.
requirements.original: Enumerated names with an associated value list shall only be used as values together with a specific integer value, which shall be one from the associated list, in parenthesis after the name.

requirements.subject: ent:enumerated-value
requirements.canonical: An enumerated value with an associated integer value list MAY be used as a template of the enumerated type by adding a list of integer templates and ranges in parentheses after its name.
requirements.original: They can be used as a template of the enumerated type by adding a list of integer template(s) and ranges in parenthesis after the name.

requirements.subject: ent:associated-integer-value
requirements.canonical: For an enumerated value with no assigned value or with a specific integer value assigned, the associated integer value SHALL NOT be used directly.
requirements.original: For enumerated values with no value assigned or with a specific integer value assigned, the user shall not directly use associated integer values, but can access them and convert integer values into enumerated values by using the predefined functions enum2int and int2enum (see clauses 16.1.2, C.1.30 and C.1.4).

requirements.subject: ent:fn-enum2int
requirements.canonical: The integer value associated with an enumerated value MAY be accessed using the predefined function `enum2int`, and an integer value MAY be converted into an enumerated value using the predefined function `int2enum`.
requirements.original: For enumerated values with no value assigned or with a specific integer value assigned, the user shall not directly use associated integer values, but can access them and convert integer values into enumerated values by using the predefined functions enum2int and int2enum (see clauses 16.1.2, C.1.30 and C.1.4).

requirements.subject: ent:associated-integer-value
requirements.canonical: The integer value associated with an enumerated value MAY also be used by the system to encode and decode enumerated values.
requirements.original: NOTE 2: The integer value also may be used by the system to encode/decode enumerated values.

requirements.subject: ent:identifier
requirements.condition: the definition is of an imported enumerated type
requirements.canonical: When a module parameter, formal parameter, constant, variable, non-parameterized template or parameterized template whose formal parameters all have default values is defined with an imported enumerated type, the name of that definition SHALL NOT be the same as any of the enumerated values of that type.
requirements.original: When a TTCN-3 module parameter, formal parameter, constant, variable, non-parameterized template or parameterized template with all formal parameters having default values of an imported enumerated type is defined, the name of that definition shall not be the same as any of the enumerated values of that type.

requirements.subject: ent:ttcn3-language
requirements.canonical: The TTCN-3 language IS defined to support the union type.
requirements.original: TTCN-3 supports the union type.

requirements.subject: ent:union-type
requirements.canonical: A union type IS a collection of alternatives, each identified by an identifier.
requirements.original: The union type is a collection of alternatives, each one identified by an identifier.

requirements.subject: ent:union-value
requirements.canonical: An actual union value IS a value in which exactly one of the specified union alternatives is present.
requirements.original: Only one of the specified alternatives will ever be present in an actual union value.

requirements.subject: ent:union-type
requirements.canonical: A union type IS suited to model data that can take one of a finite number of known types.
requirements.original: Union types are useful to model data which can take one of a finite number of known types.

requirements.subject: ent:union-value
requirements.canonical: The value notation of a union value SHALL use the assignment notation.
requirements.original: The assignment notation shall be used for union-s, and the notation shall assign a value to one field only.

ambiguity.issue: Source unit is classified as example-text by the PDF conversion although it is normative prose following an example; normative is set to false per extraction rules. "union-s" is used for values of a union type.

requirements.subject: ent:assignment-notation
requirements.canonical: The assignment notation for a union value SHALL assign a value to exactly one union alternative.
requirements.original: The assignment notation shall be used for union-s, and the notation shall assign a value to one field only.

readings: The assignment notation for a union value SHALL assign a value to exactly one union alternative.
The assignment notation for a union value SHALL NOT assign values to more than one union alternative (an empty notation being allowed).
ambiguity.issue: Source unit is classified as example-text by the PDF conversion although it is normative prose following an example; normative is set to false per extraction rules. "one field only" is read as exactly one alternative (not zero).

requirements.subject: ent:union-alternative
requirements.canonical: The union alternative assigned in the assignment notation of a union value IS the chosen alternative.
requirements.original: This field becomes the chosen field.

requirements.subject: ent:not-used-symbol
requirements.canonical: The not used symbol "-" SHALL NOT be used in a union value notation.
requirements.original: Neither the not used symbol "-" nor omit is allowed in union value notations.

requirements.subject: ent:omit-keyword
requirements.canonical: `omit` SHALL NOT be used in a union value notation.
requirements.original: Neither the not used symbol "-" nor omit is allowed in union value notations.

requirements.subject: ent:value-list-notation
requirements.canonical: The value list notation SHALL NOT be used for setting values of a union type.
requirements.original: The value list notation shall not be used for setting values of union types.

requirements.subject: ent:union-alternative
requirements.canonical: A union alternative MAY be declared as the default alternative by using the `@default` modifier before the type of the alternative.
requirements.original: At most one of the union alternatives can be declared as the default alternative by using the @default modifier before the type of the alternative.

requirements.subject: ent:union-type
requirements.canonical: A union type SHALL NOT declare more than one union alternative as the default alternative.
requirements.original: At most one of the union alternatives can be declared as the default alternative by using the @default modifier before the type of the alternative.

requirements.subject: ent:union-value
requirements.condition: the union type has a default alternative
requirements.canonical: If the union type has a default alternative, a union value IS compatible with the type of the default alternative according to the special type compatibility rules of clause 6.3.2.4.
requirements.original: For unions with a default alternative, special type compatibility rules apply (see clause 6.3.2.4) which allow using the union value as compatible with the type of the default alternative.

requirements.subject: ent:assignment-notation
requirements.condition: the union's default alternative is to be chosen
requirements.canonical: If the default alternative of a union type is to be chosen, the assignment notation NEED NOT be used to denote a value of the union type.
requirements.original: Therefore, the assignment notation does not have to be used to denote a value of the union type if the union's default alternative is to be chosen.

requirements.subject: ent:default-alternative-selection
requirements.condition: the default alternative is the chosen alternative
requirements.canonical: If the default alternative of a union value is chosen, the default alternative selection (dot notation with the alternative identifier) NEED NOT be used to access the default alternative.
requirements.original: Also, the default alternative selection does not have to be used to access the default alternative, if it is chosen.

requirements.subject: ent:list-of-effective-fields
requirements.canonical: The list of effective fields of a union type IS defined to contain all alternative identifiers of the union type.
requirements.original: The list of effective fields of a union contains all alternative identifiers of the union.

requirements.subject: ent:list-of-effective-fields
requirements.condition: the union contains a default alternative of a record or set type
requirements.canonical: If a union type has a default alternative of a record type or set type, the list of effective fields of the union type IS defined to additionally contain all field identifiers of that record type or set type.
requirements.original: In addition to that, if the union contains a default alternative of a record or set type, the list of effective fields contains all field identifiers of that type and if the union contains a default alternative of a union type, the list of effective fields contains the effective list of that type.

requirements.subject: ent:list-of-effective-fields
requirements.condition: the union contains a default alternative of a union type
requirements.canonical: If a union type has a default alternative of a union type, the list of effective fields of the union type IS defined to additionally contain the list of effective fields of that union type.
requirements.original: In addition to that, if the union contains a default alternative of a record or set type, the list of effective fields contains all field identifiers of that type and if the union contains a default alternative of a union type, the list of effective fields contains the effective list of that type.
