ambiguity.issue: Source unit is classified as example-text by the PDF conversion although it is normative prose following an example; normative is set to false per extraction rules. "effective list" is used for "list of effective fields".

requirements.subject: ent:union-type
requirements.canonical: A union type SHALL satisfy the general static rules of TTCN-3 given in clause 5 in addition to the restrictions of clause 6.2.5.0.
requirements.original: In addition to the general static rules of TTCN-3 given in clause 5, the following restrictions apply:

requirements.subject: ent:list-of-effective-fields
requirements.canonical: All identifiers in the list of effective fields of a union type SHALL be distinct.
requirements.original: a) All identifiers in the list of effective fields shall be distinct.

requirements.subject: ent:default-alternative
requirements.canonical: The default alternative of a union type SHALL NOT be of the anytype.
requirements.original: b) The @default alternative shall not be of the anytype.

requirements.subject: ent:union-alternative
requirements.canonical: A union alternative SHALL be referenced by the dot notation TypeIdOrExpression.AlternativeId.
requirements.original: Alternatives of a union type shall be referenced by the dot notation TypeIdOrExpression.AlternativeId, where TypeIdOrExpression resolves to the name of a union type or an expression of a union type such as variable, formal parameter, module parameter, constant, template, or function invocation.

requirements.subject: ent:dot-notation
requirements.canonical: In a reference to a union alternative, TypeIdOrExpression SHALL resolve to the name of a union type or to an expression of a union type (e.g. a variable, formal parameter, module parameter, constant, template or function invocation).
requirements.original: Alternatives of a union type shall be referenced by the dot notation TypeIdOrExpression.AlternativeId, where TypeIdOrExpression resolves to the name of a union type or an expression of a union type such as variable, formal parameter, module parameter, constant, template, or function invocation.

requirements.subject: ent:dot-notation
requirements.canonical: In a reference to a union alternative, AlternativeId SHALL resolve to the name of an alternative of the union type.
requirements.original: AlternativeId shall resolve to the name of an alternative in the union type or in case of an anytype value or template AlternativeId shall resolve to a known type name or a known type name qualified with a module name.

requirements.subject: ent:dot-notation
requirements.condition: the value or template is of the anytype
requirements.canonical: If the referenced value or template is of the anytype, AlternativeId SHALL resolve to a known type name or to a known type name qualified with a module name.
requirements.original: AlternativeId shall resolve to the name of an alternative in the union type or in case of an anytype value or template AlternativeId shall resolve to a known type name or a known type name qualified with a module name.

requirements.subject: ent:union-alternative
requirements.canonical: A union alternative SHALL NOT reference the union type definition it belongs to.
requirements.original: Alternatives of union type definitions shall not reference themselves.

readings: A union alternative SHALL NOT be of the enclosing union type itself.
The type of a union alternative SHALL NOT refer, directly or indirectly, to the enclosing union type.
ambiguity.issue: It is unclear whether only direct self-reference (alternative of the enclosing union type itself, giving an infinite type) is forbidden or also indirect recursion through other types; the direct reading is chosen since recursive types via e.g. record of are allowed elsewhere.

requirements.subject: ent:union-alternative
requirements.condition: an alternative is referenced by the dot notation
requirements.canonical: If a union alternative of a union type or of a subtype of a union type is referenced by the dot notation, the type of the reference IS the set of values allowed by the constraints of the alternative declaration only, and constraints applied to the union type itself are ignored.
requirements.original: If an alternative in a union type or a subtype of a union type is referenced by the dot notation, the resulting type is the set of values allowed for that alternative imposed by the constraints of the alternative declaration itself (i.e. any constraints applied to the union type itself are ignored).

requirements.subject: ent:error
requirements.condition: the referenced alternative is not the currently chosen alternative
requirements.canonical: When a union alternative is referenced on the right hand side of an assignment and the referenced alternative is not the chosen alternative, an error SHALL occur.
requirements.original: When an alternative of a union type is referenced on the right hand side of an assignment an error shall occur if the referenced alternative is not the currently chosen alternative or if the referenced union field or value is omitted or uninitialized.

requirements.subject: ent:error
requirements.condition: the referenced union field or value is omitted or uninitialized
requirements.canonical: When a union alternative is referenced on the right hand side of an assignment and the referenced union field or union value is omitted or uninitialized, an error SHALL occur.
requirements.original: When an alternative of a union type is referenced on the right hand side of an assignment an error shall occur if the referenced alternative is not the currently chosen alternative or if the referenced union field or value is omitted or uninitialized.

requirements.subject: ent:union-alternative
requirements.canonical: When a union alternative is referenced on the left hand side of an assignment, the referenced alternative SHALL become the chosen alternative.
requirements.original: When referencing an alternative of a union type on the left hand side of an assignment, the referenced alternative shall become the chosen one.

requirements.subject: ent:union-alternative
requirements.condition: the reference contains alternatives of nested unions
requirements.canonical: When a reference on the left hand side of an assignment contains alternatives of nested union values, all referenced alternatives SHALL become the chosen alternatives recursively.
requirements.original: This rule shall apply recursively if the reference contains alternatives of nested unions, choosing all the referenced alternatives.

requirements.subject: ent:union-alternative
requirements.condition: the union value or field is uninitialized or omitted
requirements.canonical: When an alternative of an uninitialized union value or field, or of an omitted field (including a field omitted at a higher level of the embedding hierarchy), is referenced on the left hand side of an assignment, the reference SHALL be expanded recursively up to and including the depth of the referenced alternative.
requirements.original: When referencing an alternative of an uninitialized union value or field or omitted field (including omitting a field at a higher level of the embedding hierarchy) on the left hand side of an assignment, the reference shall recursively be expanded up to and including the depth of the referenced alternative as follows:

requirements.subject: ent:union-alternative
requirements.canonical: When a value or value field of a union type is expanded, the union alternative referenced in the dot notation IS made the chosen alternative.
requirements.original: a) When expanding a value or value field of union type, the alternative referenced in the dot notation becomes the chosen one.

requirements.subject: ent:left-hand-side-of-assignment
requirements.canonical: When expanding a left hand side reference to a union alternative, the expansion of record, record of, set, set of and array values and intermediate fields SHALL follow the rules of item a) of clauses 6.2.1.1 and 6.2.7, and of clause 6.2.2.1, correspondingly.
requirements.original: b) Expansion of record, record of, set, set of, and array values and intermediate fields shall follow the rules of item a) in clauses 6.2.1.1 and 6.2.7, and clause 6.2.2.1 correspondingly.

readings: Record and set values follow clause 6.2.1.1 a), record of and set of values follow clause 6.2.2.1, array values follow clause 6.2.7 a).
All listed kinds of values follow the rules of all three referenced clauses.
ambiguity.issue: Source unit is classified as example-text by the PDF conversion although it is normative prose following an example; normative is set to false per extraction rules. The mapping of types to referenced clauses ("correspondingly") is not explicit; clause 6.2.1.1 covers record (and by reference set) types, 6.2.2.1 record of/set of, and 6.2.7 arrays, which is the chosen reading.

requirements.subject: ent:right-hand-side-of-assignment
requirements.canonical: At the end of the expansion, the value of the right hand side of the assignment SHALL be assigned to the referenced union alternative.
requirements.original: c) At the end of the expansion, the value at the right hand side of the assignment shall be assigned to the referenced alternative.

requirements.subject: ent:optional-keyword
requirements.canonical: The `optional` keyword SHALL NOT be used for a union alternative.
requirements.original: Optional fields are not allowed for the union type, which means that the optional keyword shall not be used with union types.

ambiguity.issue: "Optional fields" and "used with union types" refer to union alternatives.

requirements.subject: ent:union-type
requirements.canonical: A union type definition MAY contain nested type definitions for the types of its union alternatives, following the mechanism for record types of clause 6.2.1.3.
requirements.original: TTCN-3 supports the definition of types for union alternatives nested within the union definition, similar to the mechanism for record types described in clause 6.2.1.3.

requirements.subject: ent:union-type
requirements.canonical: A union type definition MAY contain embedded fields, following the mechanism for record types of clause 6.2.1.4.
requirements.original: Embedded Fields with the union definition are similar to the mechanism for record types described in clause 6.2.1.4.

readings: The rules for embedded fields of record types in clause 6.2.1.4 apply unchanged to union types.
Embedded fields in union types follow analogous but not identical (unspecified) rules.
ambiguity.issue: "similar to" does not state whether the rules of clause 6.2.1.4 apply unchanged; the reading that they apply unchanged is chosen.

requirements.subject: ent:anytype
requirements.canonical: The anytype IS a shorthand for the union of all known data types and the address type in a TTCN-3 module.
requirements.original: The special type anytype is defined as a shorthand for the union of all known data types and the address type in a TTCN-3 module.

requirements.subject: ent:anytype
requirements.condition: the address type has been explicitly defined within the module
requirements.canonical: If the address type is explicitly defined within a module, the anytype of that module SHALL include the address type as an alternative.
requirements.original: The address type shall be included if it has been explicitly defined within that module.

readings: The anytype of a module SHALL include the address type only if the address type is defined in that module.
The anytype of a module SHALL include the address type if it is defined in or imported into that module.
ambiguity.issue: It is unclear whether an address type imported into the module (rather than defined in it) is included; the reading "defined in the module itself" is chosen as it is literal.

requirements.subject: ent:anytype
requirements.canonical: Each field name of the anytype SHALL be the name of the corresponding type, identifying the field uniquely.
requirements.original: The fieldnames of the anytype shall be uniquely identified by the corresponding type names.

requirements.subject: ent:anytype
requirements.condition: the imported type name clashes
requirements.canonical: An imported type whose name clashes with an identifier of a definition in the importing module or with an identifier imported from a third module CANNOT be reached via the anytype of the importing module.
requirements.original: NOTE 1: As a result of this requirement imported types with clashing names (either with an identifier of a definition in the importing module or with an identifier imported from a third module) cannot be reached via the anytype of the importing module.

requirements.subject: ent:anytype
requirements.canonical: The anytype IS defined locally for each module.
requirements.original: The anytype is defined locally for each module and (like the other predefined types) cannot be directly imported by another module.

requirements.subject: ent:import-statement
requirements.canonical: An import statement SHALL NOT directly import the anytype of another module.
requirements.original: The anytype is defined locally for each module and (like the other predefined types) cannot be directly imported by another module.

requirements.subject: ent:user-defined-type
requirements.canonical: A user-defined type of the type anytype MAY be imported by another module.
requirements.original: However, a user defined type of the type anytype can be imported by another module.

requirements.subject: ent:import-statement
requirements.canonical: Importing a user-defined type of the type anytype IS the means by which all types of the module where it is declared become accessible (as its alternatives) in the importing module.
requirements.original: The effect of this is that all types of that module are imported.

readings: Importing a user-defined type of the type anytype makes all types of the exporting module reachable as alternatives of that user-defined type.
Importing a user-defined type of the type anytype makes all types of the exporting module visible as definitions in the importing module.
ambiguity.issue: It is unclear whether the types become visible as importable definitions in the importing module or are only reachable as alternatives of the imported user-defined type; the latter reading is chosen, consistent with NOTE 2.

requirements.subject: ent:user-defined-type
requirements.canonical: A user-defined type of the type anytype IS a type containing all types imported into the module where it is declared.
requirements.original: NOTE 2: The user-defined type of anytype "contains" all types imported into the module where it is declared.

requirements.subject: ent:import-statement
requirements.canonical: A test suite writer SHOULD exercise due caution when importing a user-defined type of the type anytype into a module, as this may cause side effects.
requirements.original: Importing such a user-defined type into a module may cause side effects and hence due caution should be given to such cases.

requirements.subject: ent:array
requirements.canonical: An array IS a shorthand notation to specify a record of type.
requirements.original: Arrays can be used in TTCN-3 as a shorthand notation to specify record of types.

requirements.subject: ent:array
requirements.canonical: An array MAY be specified at the point of a variable declaration, formal parameter declaration or function return value declaration.
requirements.original: They may be specified also at the point of a variable, formal parameter or function return value declaration.

requirements.subject: ent:array
requirements.canonical: An array MAY be declared as single-dimensional or multi-dimensional.
requirements.original: Arrays may be declared as single or multi-dimensional.

requirements.subject: ent:array-dimension
requirements.canonical: An array dimension SHALL be specified using a constant expression.
requirements.original: Array dimensions shall be specified using constant expressions, which shall evaluate to a positive integer values.

requirements.subject: ent:constant-expression
requirements.canonical: A constant expression specifying an array dimension SHALL evaluate to a positive integer value.
requirements.original: Array dimensions shall be specified using constant expressions, which shall evaluate to a positive integer values.

requirements.subject: ent:constant
requirements.canonical: A constant used in a constant expression specifying an array dimension SHALL meet the restrictions of clause 10.
requirements.original: Constants used in the constant expressions shall meet with the restrictions in clause 10.

requirements.subject: ent:index-notation
requirements.canonical: An array element IS accessed by means of the index notation ([]).
requirements.original: Array elements are accessed by means of the index notation ([]), which shall specify a valid index within the array's range.

requirements.subject: ent:index-notation
requirements.canonical: The index notation used to access an array element SHALL specify a valid index within the array's range.
requirements.original: Array elements are accessed by means of the index notation ([]), which shall specify a valid index within the array's range.

requirements.subject: ent:array-element
requirements.canonical: An individual element of a multi-dimensional array CAN be accessed by repeated use of the index notation.
requirements.original: Individual elements of multi-dimensional arrays can be accessed by repeated use of the index notation.

requirements.subject: ent:index-notation
requirements.canonical: An array or record of integer restricted to a single size MAY be used in the index notation as a short-hand for the repeated index notation.
requirements.original: An array or record of integer restricted to a single size can be used in the index notation as a short-hand for the repeated index notation.

readings: An integer array or record of integer with a fixed length MAY be used as index, its length being equal to the number of indexed dimensions.
An integer array or record of integer with a fixed length not exceeding the number of dimensions MAY be used as index, yielding an array slice.
ambiguity.issue: Source unit is classified as example-text by the PDF conversion although it is normative prose following an example; normative is set to false per extraction rules. "restricted to a single size" is read as a fixed length restriction; it is not stated whether that size must equal the number of dimensions of the indexed array.

requirements.subject: ent:error
requirements.canonical: Accessing an element outside the array's range SHALL cause a compile-time error or a test case error.
requirements.original: Accessing elements outside the array's range will cause a compile-time or test case error.

requirements.subject: ent:array-dimension
requirements.canonical: An array dimension MAY be specified using a range.
requirements.original: Array dimensions may also be specified using ranges (with inclusive boundaries only).

requirements.subject: ent:index-range
requirements.canonical: A range specifying an array dimension SHALL have inclusive boundaries only.
requirements.original: Array dimensions may also be specified using ranges (with inclusive boundaries only).

requirements.subject: ent:index-range
requirements.canonical: The lower and upper value of a range specifying an array dimension IS the lower and upper index value of that dimension, respectively.
requirements.original: In such cases, the lower and upper values of the range syntax define the lower and upper index values.

requirements.subject: ent:index-range
requirements.canonical: The upper value of a range specifying an array dimension SHALL NOT be less than the corresponding lower value.
requirements.original: The upper value shall not be lesser than the corresponding lower value.

requirements.subject: ent:array
requirements.condition: the array dimension is specified using a range
requirements.canonical: An array whose dimension is specified by a range IS equivalent to a record of type with a fixed length restriction of (upper bound - lower bound + 1), with indexing starting from the lower bound.
requirements.original: Such an array is corresponding to a record of with a fixed length restriction computed as the difference between upper and lower index bound plus 1 and indexing starting from the lower bound of the array definition.

requirements.subject: ent:array
requirements.canonical: An array type with a variable number of elements CANNOT be defined.
requirements.original: NOTE: It is not possible to define an array type with a variable amount of elements.

requirements.subject: ent:array
requirements.canonical: An unlimited array with a lower bound on the array index CANNOT be defined.
requirements.original: Neither is it possible to define an unlimited array with a lower bound on the array index.

requirements.subject: ent:array-element
requirements.canonical: The value of an array element SHALL be compatible with the corresponding variable or type declaration.
requirements.original: The values of array elements shall be compatible with the corresponding variable or type declaration.

requirements.subject: ent:array-element
requirements.canonical: Values of array elements MAY be assigned individually by a value list notation or index notation, or several or all at once by a value list notation or index assignment notation.
requirements.original: Values may be assigned individually by a value list notation or index notation or more than one or all at once by a value list notation or index assignment notation.

ambiguity.issue: Source unit is classified as example-text by the PDF conversion although it is normative prose following an example; normative is set to false per extraction rules. "index assignment notation" is not a defined term; the assignment notation with indexes (clause 6.2.2.4) is meant.

requirements.subject: ent:array
requirements.canonical: The value list notation and assignment notation for an array IS subject to the rules of clause 6.2.2.4.
requirements.original: For using the value list or assignment notation for arrays, the rules described in clause 6.2.2.4 are valid for arrays as well.

requirements.subject: ent:index-notation
requirements.canonical: The index notation MAY be used on both the right hand side and the left hand side of an assignment.
requirements.original: Index notation can be used on both the right-hand side and left-hand side of assignments.

requirements.subject: ent:array-index
requirements.canonical: The index of the first element of an array SHALL be zero, or the lower bound of the index range if an index range has been given.
requirements.original: The index of the first element shall be zero or the lower bound if an index range has been given.

requirements.subject: ent:array-index
requirements.canonical: An array index SHALL NOT exceed the limitations given by the length or by the upper bound of the index range.
requirements.original: The index shall not exceed the limitations given by either the length or the upper bound of the index.

requirements.subject: ent:error
requirements.condition: the indexed element is undefined
requirements.canonical: If the value of the array element indicated by the index on the right hand side of an assignment is undefined, an error SHALL be caused.
requirements.original: If the value of the element indicated by the index at the right-hand of an assignment is undefined or if the index notation is applied to an uninitialized or omitted array value on the right hand side of an assignment, error shall be caused.

requirements.subject: ent:error
requirements.condition: the array value is uninitialized or omitted
requirements.canonical: If the index notation is applied to an uninitialized or omitted array value on the right hand side of an assignment, an error SHALL be caused.
requirements.original: If the value of the element indicated by the index at the right-hand of an assignment is undefined or if the index notation is applied to an uninitialized or omitted array value on the right hand side of an assignment, error shall be caused.

requirements.subject: ent:error
requirements.canonical: Sending an array value with undefined elements SHALL cause an error.
requirements.original: Sending an array value with undefined elements shall cause an error.

requirements.subject: ent:array-element
requirements.canonical: An array element that is not set explicitly IS undefined.
requirements.original: All elements in an array value that are not set explicitly are undefined.

requirements.subject: ent:left-hand-side-of-assignment
requirements.canonical: When an element of an uninitialized array value or field or of an omitted field is referenced on the left hand side of an assignment, the rules for record of values of clause 6.2.2.4 SHALL apply.
requirements.original: When referencing an element of an uninitialized array value or field or omitted field on the left hand side of an assignment, the rules for record of values specified in clause 6.2.2.4 apply.

requirements.subject: ent:array-dimension
requirements.canonical: When assigning a value to a multi-dimensional array, each dimension that is assigned SHALL resolve to a set of values enclosed in curly braces.
requirements.original: For assigning values to multi-dimensional arrays, each dimension that is assigned shall resolve to a set of values enclosed in curly braces.

requirements.subject: ent:array-dimension
requirements.canonical: In a value for a multi-dimensional array, the leftmost dimension IS the outermost structure of the value and the rightmost dimension IS the innermost structure.
requirements.original: When specifying values for multi-dimensional arrays, the leftmost dimension corresponds to the outermost structure of the value, and the rightmost dimension to the innermost structure.

requirements.subject: ent:array-slice
requirements.canonical: An array slice of a multi-dimensional array MAY be used.
requirements.original: The use of array slices of multi-dimensional arrays, i.e. when the number of indexes of the array value is less than the number of dimensions in the corresponding array definition, is allowed.

requirements.subject: ent:array-slice
requirements.canonical: An array slice IS a reference to a multi-dimensional array value with fewer indexes than the number of dimensions in the corresponding array definition.
requirements.original: The use of array slices of multi-dimensional arrays, i.e. when the number of indexes of the array value is less than the number of dimensions in the corresponding array definition, is allowed.

requirements.subject: ent:array-slice
requirements.canonical: The indexes of an array slice SHALL correspond to the dimensions of the array definition from left to right.
requirements.original: Indexes of array slices shall correspond to the dimensions of the array definition from left to right (i.e. the first index of the slice corresponds to the first dimension of the definition).

requirements.subject: ent:array-slice
requirements.canonical: The indexes of an array slice SHALL conform to the related dimensions of the array definition.
requirements.original: Slice indexes shall conform to the related array definition dimensions.

requirements.subject: ent:altstep
requirements.canonical: An altstep MAY be activated as a default to capture recurring behaviour.
requirements.original: TTCN-3 allows the activation of altsteps (see clause 16.2.1) as defaults to capture recurring behaviour.

requirements.subject: ent:default-reference
requirements.canonical: A default reference IS a unique reference to an activated default.
requirements.original: Default references are unique references to activated defaults.

requirements.subject: ent:test-component
requirements.canonical: A test component SHALL generate a unique default reference when an altstep is activated as a default.
requirements.original: Such a unique default reference is generated by a test component when an altstep is activated as a default, i.e. a default reference is the result of an activate operation (see clause 20.5.2).

requirements.subject: ent:default-reference
requirements.canonical: A default reference IS the result of an `activate` operation.
requirements.original: Such a unique default reference is generated by a test component when an altstep is activated as a default, i.e. a default reference is the result of an activate operation (see clause 20.5.2).

requirements.subject: ent:default-reference
requirements.canonical: A default reference IS of the special predefined type `default`.
requirements.original: Default references have the special and predefined type default.

requirements.subject: ent:variable
requirements.canonical: A variable of type `default` MAY be used to handle activated defaults in a test component.
requirements.original: Variables of type default can be used to handle activated defaults in test components.

requirements.subject: ent:null-value
requirements.canonical: The special value `null` IS an unspecific default reference.
requirements.original: The special value null represents an unspecific default reference, e.g. can be used for the initialization of variables of default type.

requirements.subject: ent:null-value
requirements.canonical: The special value `null` MAY be used for the initialization of a variable of type `default`.
requirements.original: The special value null represents an unspecific default reference, e.g. can be used for the initialization of variables of default type.

requirements.subject: ent:default-reference
requirements.canonical: A default reference IS used in a `deactivate` operation to identify the default to be deactivated.
requirements.original: Default references are used in deactivate operations (see clause 20.5.3) in order to identify the default to be deactivated.

requirements.subject: ent:default-reference
requirements.canonical: A default reference IS meaningful only within the test component instance in which the default was activated.
requirements.original: Default references have meaning only within the test component instances they are activated, i.e. a default reference assigned to a default variable in test component instance "a1" of type "A" has no meaning in test component instance "a2" of type "A".

readings: Using a default reference in a test component instance other than the one where it was activated has no effect.
Using a default reference in a test component instance other than the one where it was activated SHALL cause an error.
ambiguity.issue: "has no meaning" does not state the observable consequence of using a default reference in another test component instance; no error behaviour is assumed in the canonical text.

requirements.subject: ent:test-system
requirements.canonical: The actual data representation of the `default` type SHALL be resolved externally by the test system.
requirements.original: The actual data representation of the default type shall be resolved externally by the test system.

requirements.subject: ent:ttcn3-language
requirements.canonical: The TTCN-3 language IS NOT restricting the implementation of a test system with respect to the handling and identification of defaults.
requirements.original: This allows abstract test cases to be specified independently of any real TTCN-3 runtime environment, in other words TTCN-3 does not restrict the implementation of a test system with respect to the handling and identification of defaults.

requirements.subject: ent:default-type
requirements.canonical: A value of the `default` type IS an object reference and follows the rules for object references.
requirements.original: Values of the default type are object references and follow specific rules for this kind of values.

requirements.subject: ent:port
requirements.canonical: A port IS the means of communication between test components and between test components and the test system interface.
requirements.original: Ports facilitate communication between test components and between test components and the test system interface.

requirements.subject: ent:ttcn3-language
requirements.canonical: The TTCN-3 language IS supporting message-based ports and procedure-based ports.
requirements.original: TTCN-3 supports message-based and procedure-based ports.

requirements.subject: ent:port-type
requirements.canonical: A port type SHALL be defined as being either message-based or procedure-based.
requirements.original: Each port shall be defined as being message-based or procedure-based.

ambiguity.issue: The sentence says 'each port' but the kind is fixed in the port type definition (see next sentence).

requirements.subject: ent:message-based-port
requirements.canonical: A message-based port type definition SHALL be identified by the keyword `message`.
requirements.original: Message-based ports shall be identified by the keyword message and procedure-based ports shall be identified by the keyword `procedure` within the associated port type definition.

requirements.subject: ent:procedure-based-port
requirements.canonical: A procedure-based port type definition SHALL be identified by the keyword `procedure`.
requirements.original: Message-based ports shall be identified by the keyword message and procedure-based ports shall be identified by the keyword `procedure` within the associated port type definition.

requirements.subject: ent:port
requirements.canonical: A port IS bidirectional.
requirements.original: Ports are bidirectional.

requirements.subject: ent:port-direction
requirements.canonical: The communication direction of a port type list IS specified by the keyword `in` (in direction), `out` (out direction) or `inout` (both directions).
requirements.original: The directions are specified by the keywords `in` (for the in direction), `out` (for the out direction) and inout (for both directions).

requirements.subject: ent:in-list
requirements.canonical: The operations `getcall`, `reply` and `raise` MAY be applied to a signature present in the in list of a procedure-based port.
requirements.original: Operations allowed on a procedure present in the incoming port list are ` `getcall`, `reply` and `raise`.

ambiguity.issue: Only part of the rule is stated: it is unclear whether these are the only operations allowed, and the wording 'procedure' is used for signature; the sentence also contains a stray backtick.
readings: The operations `getcall`, `reply` and `raise` MAY be applied to a signature present in the in list of a procedure-based port.
Only the operations `getcall`, `reply` and `raise` SHALL be applied to a signature present only in the in list of a procedure-based port.

requirements.subject: ent:out-list
requirements.canonical: The operations `call`, `getreply` and `catch` MAY be applied to a signature present in the out list of a procedure-based port.
requirements.original: Operations allowed on a procedure present in the outcoming port list are `call`, `getreply` and `catch`.

ambiguity.issue: The sentence uses 'procedure' for signature and 'outcoming port list' (a typo) for the out list.

requirements.subject: ent:port-direction
requirements.condition: the port is not a test system interface port
requirements.canonical: The communication direction of a port SHALL be seen from the point of view of the test component owning the port.
requirements.original: Directions shall be seen from the point of view of the test component owning the port with the exception of the test system interface, where directions shall be seen from the point of view of the test component port mapped to the test system interface port.

requirements.subject: ent:port-direction
requirements.condition: the port is a port of the test system interface
requirements.canonical: The communication direction of a test system interface port SHALL be seen from the point of view of the test component port mapped to the test system interface port.
requirements.original: Directions shall be seen from the point of view of the test component owning the port with the exception of the test system interface, where directions shall be seen from the point of view of the test component port mapped to the test system interface port.

requirements.subject: ent:in-list
requirements.canonical: The in list of a test system interface port IS containing the message types and signatures for which the mapped test component port allows the operations `receive`, `trigger`, `getcall`, `reply` or `raise`.
requirements.original: The in list of the test system interface port contains message or procedure for which the mapped test component port allows the following operations: `receive`, `trigger`, `getcall`, `reply` or `raise`.

ambiguity.issue: 'contains' may describe what the in list must contain (a requirement on the declaration) or a consequence of the direction rule; also 'message or procedure' should be message types or signatures.
readings: The in list of a test system interface port IS containing the message types and signatures for which the mapped test component port allows `receive`, `trigger`, `getcall`, `reply` or `raise`.
The in list of a test system interface port SHALL contain every message type and signature for which a mapped test component port allows `receive`, `trigger`, `getcall`, `reply` or `raise`.

requirements.subject: ent:out-list
requirements.canonical: The out list of a test system interface port IS containing the message types and signatures for which the mapped test component port allows the operations `send`, `call`, `getreply` or `catch`.
requirements.original: The out list of the test system interface port contains message or procedure for which the mapped test component port allow the following operations: `send`, `call`, `getreplay` or `catch`.

ambiguity.issue: 'contains' may describe a requirement on the declaration or a consequence; 'getreplay' is a typo for `getreply`; 'message or procedure' should be message types or signatures.
readings: The out list of a test system interface port IS containing the message types and signatures for which the mapped test component port allows `send`, `call`, `getreply` or `catch`.
The out list of a test system interface port SHALL contain every message type and signature for which a mapped test component port allows `send`, `call`, `getreply` or `catch`.

requirements.subject: ent:port-type
requirements.canonical: A port type definition SHALL have one or more lists indicating the allowed message types or signatures together with the allowed communication direction.
requirements.original: Each port type definition shall have one or more lists indicating the allowed collection of (message) types or procedure signatures together with the allowed communication direction.

requirements.subject: ent:port-type
requirements.canonical: A port type MAY have one `map param` declaration indicating the allowed additional parameters of the `map` operation.
requirements.original: For configuration purposes the port type may have one **map param** and **one unmap param** declaration indicating the allowed additional parameters for the respective operation.

requirements.subject: ent:port-type
requirements.canonical: A port type MAY have one `unmap param` declaration indicating the allowed additional parameters of the `unmap` operation.
requirements.original: For configuration purposes the port type may have one **map param** and **one unmap param** declaration indicating the allowed additional parameters for the respective operation.

requirements.subject: ent:formal-parameter
requirements.canonical: A formal parameter of a `map param` or `unmap param` declaration SHALL be a value parameter.
requirements.original: These formal parameters shall be value parameters.

requirements.subject: ent:in-list
requirements.condition: a signature is defined in the out direction of a procedure-based port
requirements.canonical: If a signature is defined in the out direction of a procedure-based port, the types of all its `inout` and `out` parameters, its return type and its exception types ARE automatically part of the in direction of that port.
requirements.original: Whenever a signature (see also clause 14) is defined in the out direction of a procedure-based port, the types of all its inout and out parameters, its return type and its exception types are automatically part of the in direction of this port.

requirements.subject: ent:out-list
requirements.condition: a signature is defined in the in direction of a procedure-based port
requirements.canonical: If a signature is defined in the in direction of a procedure-based port, the types of all its `inout` and `out` parameters, its return type and its exception types ARE automatically part of the out direction of that port.
requirements.original: Whenever a signature is defined in the in direction for a procedure-based port, the types of all its inout and out parameters, its return type and its exception types are automatically part of the out direction of this port.

requirements.subject: ent:port
requirements.canonical: A port used for communication with the SUT CAN need to address specific entities within the SUT.
requirements.original: Ports used for the communication with the SUT may need to address specific entities within the SUT.

requirements.subject: ent:sut
requirements.canonical: The SUT CAN support several address schemes at different ports.
requirements.original: In addition, several address schemes may be supported by one SUT at different ports.

requirements.subject: ent:port-type
requirements.canonical: An address type MAY be bound to a port type.
requirements.original: To support such addressing schemes, TTCN-3 allows to bind an address type to a port.

ambiguity.issue: The text says the address type is bound to a 'port', while it is declared in the port type.

requirements.subject: ent:address-type
requirements.canonical: A value of the address type bound to a port MAY be used for addressing purposes in communication operations.
requirements.original: Values of this type may be used for addressing purposes in communication operations (see clause 22.1) and be stored in variables.

requirements.subject: ent:address-type
requirements.canonical: A value of the address type bound to a port MAY be stored in a variable.
requirements.original: Values of this type may be used for addressing purposes in communication operations (see clause 22.1) and be stored in variables.

requirements.subject: ent:message-based-port
requirements.canonical: A message-based port type definition has the syntax `type port` PortTypeIdentifier `message` "{" followed by any sequence of `address` Type ";", `map param` "(" FormalValuePar list ")", `unmap param` "(" FormalValuePar list ")" and (`in` | `out` | `inout`) MessageType list ";" entries, and "}".
requirements.original:
type port PortTypeIdentifier message "{"
     { (address Type ";") |
      (map param "(" { FormalValuePar [","] }+ ")") |
      (unmap param "(" { FormalValuePar [","] }+ ")") |
      ((in | out | inout) { MessageType [ "," ] }+ ";") } 
  "}"

requirements.subject: ent:procedure-based-port
requirements.canonical: A procedure-based port type definition has the syntax `type port` PortTypeIdentifier `procedure` "{" followed by any sequence of `address` Type ";", `map param` "(" FormalValuePar list ")", `unmap param` "(" FormalValuePar list ")" and (`in` | `out` | `inout`) Signature list ";" entries, and "}".
requirements.original:
type port PortTypeIdentifier procedure "{"
     { (address Type ";" ) |
      (map param "(" { FormalValuePar [","] }+ ")") |
      (unmap param "(" { FormalValuePar [","] }+ ")") |
      ((in | out | inout) { Signature [ "," ] }+ ";") } 
  "}"

requirements.subject: ent:port-type
requirements.canonical: A constant, variable or formal parameter MAY be of a port type.
requirements.original: TTCN-3 allows to define constants, variables and parameters of a port type.

ambiguity.issue: 'parameters' is used for formal parameters.

requirements.subject: ent:port-type-value
requirements.canonical: A constant, variable or formal parameter of a port type CAN contain a reference to an existing component port or the special value `null`.
requirements.original: These constants, variables or parameters can contain a reference to an existing component port or a special value null.

requirements.subject: ent:null-value
requirements.canonical: The special value `null` of a port type IS representing an unspecified port reference, i.e. the reference to no port.
requirements.original: The special value null represents an unspecified port reference, i.e. it can be used to explicitly allow the referencing of no port.

requirements.subject: ent:port-type-value
requirements.canonical: A port type value IS an object reference and follows the rules for object references.
requirements.original: Port type values are object references and follow specific rules for this kind of values.

ambiguity.issue: 'specific rules for this kind of values' is not referenced to a clause.
readings: A port type value IS an object reference and follows the rules for object references defined in this standard.
A port type value IS an object reference; the rules applying to it are not specified in this clause.

requirements.subject: ent:port-type
requirements.canonical: A port type SHALL have at most one address type bound to it.
requirements.original: a) At most one address type shall be bound to a port type.

requirements.subject: ent:port-type
requirements.canonical: A port type SHALL have at most one map parameter list defined.
requirements.original: b) At most one map parameter list shall be defined for a port type.

requirements.subject: ent:port-type
requirements.canonical: A port type SHALL have at most one unmap parameter list defined.
requirements.original: c) At most one unmap parameter list shall be defined for a port type.

requirements.subject: ent:formal-parameter
requirements.canonical: A formal parameter of a `map param` or `unmap param` declaration SHALL be a value parameter of a data type.
requirements.original: d) Formal parameters of map param and unmap param declarations shall be value parameters of a data type.

requirements.subject: ent:message-type
requirements.canonical: A MessageType in a message-based port type definition SHALL be a reference to a data type.
requirements.original: e) `MessageType shall be a reference to a data type.`

requirements.subject: ent:message
requirements.canonical: The term message IS used to mean both messages defined by templates and actual values resulting from expressions.
requirements.original: NOTE: The term message is used to mean both messages as defined by templates and actual values resulting from expressions.

requirements.subject: ent:message-based-port
requirements.canonical: The list restricting what may be used on a message-based port IS a list of type names.
requirements.original: Thus, the list restricting what may be used on a message-based port is simply a list of type names.

requirements.subject: ent:component-type
requirements.canonical: A component type IS defining which ports are associated with a component.
requirements.original: The component type defines which ports are associated with a component (see figure 3).

requirements.subject: ent:port-name
requirements.canonical: A port name in a component type definition IS local to that component type, and another component type MAY have ports with the same name.
requirements.original: The port names in a component type definition are local to that component type, i.e. another component type may have ports with the same names.

requirements.subject: ent:port-name
requirements.canonical: All port names in the same component type definition SHALL be unique.
requirements.original: Port names in the same component type definition shall all have unique names.

ambiguity.issue: Unclear whether uniqueness is only among ports or among all definitions of the component type (variables, timers, ...); the general scope rules of clause 5.2 suggest the latter.
readings: All port names in the same component type definition SHALL be unique among the ports.
A port name in a component type definition SHALL be unique among all identifiers declared in that component type.

requirements.subject: ent:component-port
requirements.canonical: Unless stated otherwise, a component port IS having the same semantics as a constant of a port type.
requirements.original: If not stated otherwise, ports have the same semantics as constants of a port type.

requirements.subject: ent:component-type
requirements.canonical: A component type MAY contain declarations of constants, variables, templates and timers local to that component type.
requirements.original: It is also possible to declare constants, variables, templates and timers local to a particular component type.

requirements.subject: ent:component-type
requirements.canonical: The constants, variables, templates and timers declared in a component type ARE visible to all testcases, functions and altsteps that run on an instance of that component type.
requirements.original: These declarations are visible to all testcases, functions and altsteps that run on an instance of the given component type.

requirements.subject: ent:runs-on-clause
requirements.canonical: A testcase, function or altstep that uses the declarations of a component type SHALL explicitly state the component type in a `runs on` clause of its header.
requirements.original: This shall be explicitly stated using the runs on keyword (see clause 15.12) in the testcase, function or altstep header.

requirements.subject: ent:component-type
requirements.canonical: A component type definition IS associated with the component instance and follows the scope rules of clause 5.2.
requirements.original: Component type definitions are associated with the component instance and follow the scope rules defined in clause 5.2.

requirements.subject: ent:component-instance
requirements.canonical: Each new instance of a component type IS having its own set of constants, variables, templates and timers as specified in the component type definition, including any initial values.
requirements.original: Each new instance of a component type will thus have its own set of constants, variables, templates and timers as specified in the component type definition (including any initial values, if stated).

requirements.subject: ent:constant-expression
requirements.canonical: A constant used in the constant expression of a type declaration for a component variable, constant or port SHALL meet the restrictions of clause 10.
requirements.original: Constants used in the constant expressions of type declarations for variables, constants or ports shall meet with the restrictions in clause 10, however constants used in the constant expressions of initial values for variables, constants, templates or timers do not have to obey these restrictions.

ambiguity.issue: 'type declarations' presumably means constant expressions within the type part of a declaration (e.g. array dimensions, length restrictions); the restrictions of clause 10 are not named explicitly.
readings: A constant used in a constant expression within the type of a component variable, constant or port declaration (e.g. array size) SHALL meet the restrictions of clause 10.
A constant used in any constant expression of a component variable, constant or port declaration, except its initial value, SHALL meet the restrictions of clause 10.

requirements.subject: ent:constant-expression
requirements.canonical: A constant used in the constant expression of an initial value for a component variable, constant, template or timer NEED NOT obey the restrictions of clause 10.
requirements.original: Constants used in the constant expressions of type declarations for variables, constants or ports shall meet with the restrictions in clause 10, however constants used in the constant expressions of initial values for variables, constants, templates or timers do not have to obey these restrictions.

requirements.subject: ent:component-type
requirements.canonical: A component type definition has the syntax `type component` ComponentTypeIdentifier "{" { PortInstance | VarInstance | TimerInstance | ConstDef | TemplateDef } "}".
requirements.original:
type component ComponentTypeIdentifier "{"
     { ( PortInstance
     | VarInstance
     | TimerInstance
     | ConstDef
    | TemplateDef ) } 
  "}"

requirements.subject: ent:component-type
requirements.canonical: A component type definition IS specifying the creation, declaration and initialization of ports, component constants, variables, templates and timers during the creation of an instance of the component type.
requirements.original: Component type definitions specify the creation, declaration and initialization of ports and component constants, variables, templates and timers during the creation of an instance of a component type.

requirements.subject: ent:component-instance
requirements.canonical: An instance of a component type MAY be used as the main test component, as the test system interface or as a parallel test component.
requirements.original: These instances can be used as the main test component, as the test system interface or as a parallel test component.

requirements.subject: ent:component-instance
requirements.canonical: Every instance of a component type IS having its own new instances of the ports, constants, variables, templates and timers defined in the component type definition.
requirements.original: Every instance of a component type has its own new instances of the ports, constants, variables, templates and timers defined in the component type definition.

requirements.subject: ent:component-instance
requirements.canonical: A component instance IS an object reference and follows the rules for object references.
requirements.original: Component instances are object references and follow specific rules for this kind of values.

ambiguity.issue: 'Component instances are object references' conflates the component and the reference value to it; 'specific rules' are not referenced.
readings: A component reference value IS an object reference and follows the rules for object references.
A component instance itself IS an object, referenced through object references.

requirements.subject: ent:port-array
requirements.canonical: A component type MAY declare port arrays, including multi-dimensional port arrays.

requirements.subject: ent:component-type
requirements.canonical: A component type MAY be defined as the extension of other component types using the `extends` keyword.
requirements.original: It is possible to define component types as the extension of other component types, using the extends keyword.

requirements.subject: ent:extended-component-type
requirements.canonical: A component type extension has the syntax `type component` ComponentTypeIdentifier `extends` ComponentTypeIdentifier { "," ComponentTypeIdentifier } "{" { PortInstance | VarInstance | TimerInstance | ConstDef | TemplateDef } "}".
requirements.original:
type component ComponentTypeIdentifier extends ComponentTypeIdentifier
     { "," ComponentTypeIdentifier} "{"
     { ( PortInstance
     | VarInstance
     | TimerInstance
     | ConstDef
    | TemplateDef ) } 
  "}"

requirements.subject: ent:extended-component-type
requirements.canonical: The component type defined with `extends` IS called the extended type.
requirements.original: In such a definition, the new type definition is referred to as the extended type, and the type definition following the extends keyword is referred to as the supertype.

requirements.subject: ent:super-type
requirements.canonical: A component type following the `extends` keyword IS called the supertype.
requirements.original: In such a definition, the new type definition is referred to as the extended type, and the type definition following the extends keyword is referred to as the supertype.

ambiguity.issue: 'supertype' is used while the glossary term is 'super type'.

requirements.subject: ent:extended-component-type
requirements.canonical: An extended component type IS implicitly containing all definitions from its supertype.
requirements.original: The effect of this definition is that the extended type will implicitly also contain all definitions from the supertype.

requirements.subject: ent:effective-component-type-definition
requirements.canonical: The definition of an extended component type including all definitions implicitly contained from its supertype IS called the effective type definition.
requirements.original: It is called the effective type definition.

ambiguity.issue: 'It' may refer to the extended type or to the result of the implicit inclusion.
readings: The extended type together with the implicitly contained supertype definitions IS called the effective type definition.
The extended type definition as written IS called the effective type definition.

requirements.subject: ent:extended-component-type
requirements.canonical: A component type MAY extend several supertypes in one definition, specified as a comma-separated list of component types.
requirements.original: It is allowed to have one component type extending several supertypes in one definition, which have to be specified as a comma-separated list of types in the definition.

requirements.subject: ent:super-type
requirements.canonical: A supertype of a component type extension MAY itself be defined by means of extension.
requirements.original: Any of the supertypes may also be defined by means of extension.

requirements.subject: ent:effective-component-type-definition
requirements.canonical: The effective component type definition of an extended type IS the collection of all constant, variable, template, timer and port definitions contributed by the supertypes, determined recursively, and the definitions declared directly in the extended type.
requirements.original: The effective component type definition of the extended type is obtained as the collection of all constant, variable, template, timer and port definitions contributed by the supertypes (determined recursively if a supertype is also defined by means of an extension) and the definitions declared in the extended type directly.

requirements.subject: ent:effective-component-type-definition
requirements.canonical: The effective component type definition SHALL be free of name clashes.
requirements.original: The effective component type definition shall be name clash free.

requirements.subject: ent:name-clash
requirements.canonical: A definition contributed to the extended type by different supertypes via different extension paths IS NOT a different declaration and causes no error.
requirements.original: NOTE 1: It is not considered to be a different declaration and hence causes no error if a specific definition is contributed to the extended type by different supertypes (via different extension paths).

requirements.subject: ent:extended-component-type
requirements.canonical: The semantics of a component type with extensions IS defined by replacing each component type definition with its effective component type definition as a pre-processing step before use.
requirements.original: The semantics of component types with extensions are defined by simply replacing each component type definition by its effective component type definition as a pre-processing step prior to using it.

requirements.subject: ent:component-reference
requirements.canonical: A component reference of a component type CT1 that extends CT2 IS compatible with CT2, and testcases, functions and altsteps with `runs on` CT2 CAN be executed on it.
requirements.original: NOTE 2: For component type compatibility, this means that a component reference c of type CT1, which extends CT2, is compatible with CT2, and test cases, functions and altsteps specifying CT2 in their runs `on` clauses can be executed on c (see clause 6.3.2.7).

ambiguity.issue: 'test cases' is used for testcases.

requirements.subject: ent:extended-component-type
requirements.canonical: When defining a component type by extension, a port, variable, constant or timer identifier SHALL NOT be declared both in the supertype (directly or by means of extension) and in the extended type.
requirements.original: a) When defining component types by extension, there shall be no name clash between the definitions being taken from the supertype and the definitions being added in the extended type, i.e. there shall not be a port, variable, constant or timer identifier that is declared both in the supertype (directly or by means of extension) and the extended type.

ambiguity.issue: The list 'port, variable, constant or timer' omits templates, although templates are part of component type definitions and of the effective definition (s008).
readings: A port, variable, constant, timer or template identifier SHALL NOT be declared both in the supertype and the extended type.
Only port, variable, constant and timer identifiers SHALL NOT be declared both in the supertype and the extended type.

requirements.subject: ent:name-clash
requirements.canonical: A definition contributed to the extended type via different extension paths IS NOT a name clash between the supertype and the extended type.
requirements.original: It is not considered to be a name clash if a specific definition is contributed to the extended type via different extension paths.

requirements.subject: ent:extended-component-type
requirements.canonical: When defining a component type by extending more than one supertype, a port, variable, constant or timer identifier SHALL NOT be declared in any two of the supertypes (directly or by means of extension).
requirements.original: b) When defining component types by extending more than one parent type, there shall be no name clash between the definitions of the different supertypes, i.e. there shall not be a port, variable, constant or timer identifier that is declared in any two of the supertypes (directly or by means of extension).

ambiguity.issue: Templates are omitted from the list of definitions; 'parent type' is used for supertype.
readings: A port, variable, constant, timer or template identifier SHALL NOT be declared in any two supertypes.
Only port, variable, constant and timer identifiers SHALL NOT be declared in any two supertypes.

requirements.subject: ent:name-clash
requirements.canonical: A definition contributed to the extended type via different extension paths IS NOT a name clash between different supertypes.
requirements.original: It is not considered to be a name clash if a specific definition is contributed to the extended type via different extension paths.

requirements.subject: ent:extended-component-type
requirements.canonical: A component type defined by means of extension MAY itself be extended.
requirements.original: c) It is allowed to extend component types that are defined by means of extension, as long as no cyclic chain of definition is created.

requirements.subject: ent:extended-component-type
requirements.canonical: A component type extension SHALL NOT create a cyclic chain of definitions.
requirements.original: c) It is allowed to extend component types that are defined by means of extension, as long as no cyclic chain of definition is created.

requirements.subject: ent:component-reference
requirements.canonical: A component reference IS a unique reference to a test component created during the execution of a testcase.
requirements.original: Component references are unique references to the test components created during the execution of a test case.

requirements.subject: ent:component-reference
requirements.canonical: A component reference IS syntactically one of `system`, `mtc`, `self` or an ObjectReference.
requirements.original: system | mtc | self | ObjectReference

requirements.subject: ent:test-system
requirements.canonical: The test system SHALL generate a unique component reference at the time a test component is created.
requirements.original: A unique component reference is generated by the test system at the time when a component is created.

requirements.subject: ent:create-operation
requirements.canonical: The `create` operation IS returning the unique component reference of the created test component.
requirements.original: It is the result of a create operation (see clause 21.2.1).

requirements.subject: ent:system-operation
requirements.canonical: The `system` operation IS returning the component reference of the test system interface.
requirements.original: In addition, component references are returned by the predefined operations system (returns the component reference of the test system interface, which is automatically created when testcase execution is started), mtc (returns the component reference of the MTC, which is automatically created when testcase execution started) and self (returns the component reference of the component in which self is called).

requirements.subject: ent:test-system-interface
requirements.canonical: The test system interface IS created automatically when testcase execution is started.
requirements.original: In addition, component references are returned by the predefined operations system (returns the component reference of the test system interface, which is automatically created when testcase execution is started), mtc (returns the component reference of the MTC, which is automatically created when testcase execution started) and self (returns the component reference of the component in which self is called).

requirements.subject: ent:mtc-operation
requirements.canonical: The `mtc` operation IS returning the component reference of the MTC.
requirements.original: In addition, component references are returned by the predefined operations system (returns the component reference of the test system interface, which is automatically created when testcase execution is started), mtc (returns the component reference of the MTC, which is automatically created when testcase execution started) and self (returns the component reference of the component in which self is called).

requirements.subject: ent:mtc
requirements.canonical: The MTC IS created automatically when testcase execution is started.
requirements.original: In addition, component references are returned by the predefined operations system (returns the component reference of the test system interface, which is automatically created when testcase execution is started), mtc (returns the component reference of the MTC, which is automatically created when testcase execution started) and self (returns the component reference of the component in which self is called).

requirements.subject: ent:self-operation
requirements.canonical: The `self` operation IS returning the component reference of the test component in which `self` is called.
requirements.original: In addition, component references are returned by the predefined operations system (returns the component reference of the test system interface, which is automatically created when testcase execution is started), mtc (returns the component reference of the MTC, which is automatically created when testcase execution started) and self (returns the component reference of the component in which self is called).

requirements.subject: ent:component-reference
requirements.canonical: A component reference MAY be used in configuration operations such as `connect`, `map` and `start` to set up test configurations.
requirements.original: Component references are used in the configuration operations such as connect, map and start (see clause 21) to set-up test configurations and in the from, to and sender parts of communication operations of ports connected to test components other than the test system interface for addressing purposes (see clause 22 and figure 6).

requirements.subject: ent:component-reference
requirements.canonical: A component reference MAY be used for addressing in the `from`, `to` and `sender` parts of communication operations of ports connected to test components other than the test system interface.
requirements.original: Component references are used in the configuration operations such as connect, map and start (see clause 21) to set-up test configurations and in the from, to and sender parts of communication operations of ports connected to test components other than the test system interface for addressing purposes (see clause 22 and figure 6).

requirements.subject: ent:null-value
requirements.canonical: The special value `null` MAY be used to indicate an undefined component reference, e.g. to initialize a variable of a component type.
requirements.original: In addition, the special value null is available to indicate an undefined component reference, e.g. for the initialization of variables to handle component references.

requirements.subject: ent:test-system
requirements.canonical: The test system SHALL resolve the actual data representation of component references externally.
requirements.original: The actual data representation of component references shall be resolved externally by the test system.

requirements.subject: ent:ttcn3-language
requirements.canonical: The TTCN-3 language IS NOT restricting the implementation of a test system with respect to the handling and identification of test components.
requirements.original: This allows abstract test cases to be specified independently of any real TTCN-3 runtime environment, in other words TTCN-3 does not restrict the implementation of a test system with respect to the handling and identification of test components.

requirements.subject: ent:component-reference
requirements.canonical: A component reference IS carrying the component type information of the referenced test component.
requirements.original: A component reference includes component type information.

requirements.subject: ent:variable
requirements.canonical: A variable for handling component references SHALL be declared with the corresponding component type name as its type.
requirements.original: This means, for example, that a variable for handling component references shall use the corresponding component type name in its declaration.

requirements.subject: ent:configuration-operation
requirements.canonical: A configuration operation SHALL NOT be applied directly to an array of component references.
requirements.original: The configuration operations (see clause 21) do not work directly on arrays of components.

ambiguity.issue: 'arrays of components' is used, but TTCN-3 only has arrays of component references.

requirements.subject: ent:configuration-operation
requirements.canonical: When a configuration operation refers to a test component held in an array of component references, a specific element of the array SHALL be provided as the parameter of the operation.
requirements.original: Instead a specific element of the array shall be provided as the parameter to these operations.

requirements.subject: ent:array
requirements.canonical: The effect of an array of test components CAN be achieved by using an array of component references and assigning the result of a `create` operation to each relevant array element.
requirements.original: For components, the effect of an array is achieved by using an array of component references and assigning the relevant array element to the result of the create operation.

requirements.subject: ent:component-reference
requirements.canonical: An operator other than assignment, equality (`==`) and non-equality (`!=`) SHALL NOT be applied to a component reference.
requirements.original: a) The only operations allowed on component references are assignment, equality and non-equality.

ambiguity.issue: 'operations' is read as expression operators; component operations such as start, stop, done or running are also applied to component references and are defined in clause 21, so a literal reading would contradict them.
readings: An operator other than assignment, equality (`==`) and non-equality (`!=`) SHALL NOT be applied to a component reference.
No operation other than assignment, equality and non-equality (including component operations like `start` or `done`) SHALL be applied to a component reference.

requirements.subject: ent:component-reference
requirements.canonical: The ObjectReference of a component reference SHALL be of a component type.
requirements.original: b) The ObjectReference shall be of a component type and shall not resolve to a template.

requirements.subject: ent:component-reference
requirements.canonical: The ObjectReference of a component reference SHALL NOT resolve to a template.
requirements.original: b) The ObjectReference shall be of a component type and shall not resolve to a template.

requirements.subject: ent:sut
requirements.canonical: An SUT CAN consist of several entities which can be addressed individually.
requirements.original: An SUT may consist of several entities which can be addressed individually.

requirements.subject: ent:address-type
requirements.canonical: The global `address` type MAY be used for addressing SUT entities if only one address type is needed.
requirements.original: The global address type may be used if only one type is needed.

requirements.subject: ent:port-type
requirements.condition: several address types at different ports are needed for addressing SUT entities
requirements.canonical: If several address types are needed at different ports for addressing SUT entities, the address type used for addressing via a port instance SHALL be declared in the corresponding port type definition.
requirements.original: If several types at different ports are needed for addressing SUT entities, the type used for addressing via a port instance shall be declared in the corresponding port type definition.

requirements.subject: ent:sut-address
requirements.canonical: An SUT address used for addressing IS syntactically a TemplateInstance.
requirements.original: TemplateInstance

requirements.subject: ent:address-type
requirements.canonical: The actual data representation of the address type IS resolved by an explicit global `address` type definition in the test suite, by address type declarations in port type definitions, or externally by the test system when `address` is left as an open type.
requirements.original: The actual data representation of the global address type is resolved either by an explicit global address type definition within the test suite, address type definitions within port definitions, or externally by the test system (i.e. the address type is left as an open type within the TTCN-3 specification).

ambiguity.issue: The sentence speaks of the representation of the 'global address type' being resolved by 'address type definitions within port definitions'; the chosen reading is that it describes the three ways the address representation in general is determined.
readings: The actual data representation of the address type IS resolved by a global `address` type definition, by address declarations in port type definitions, or externally by the test system.
The actual data representation of the global `address` type IS resolved by a global definition, or, if missing, by port-type address declarations or externally.

requirements.subject: ent:sut-address
requirements.condition: an address type is bound to the port type definition
requirements.canonical: If an address type is bound to a port type definition, addressing of SUT entities in `to` and `from` directives of communication operations via instances of that port type SHALL be restricted to values of the bound address type.
requirements.original: If an address type is bound to a port type definition, addressing of SUT instances (i.e. to- and from-directives in communication operations) via instances of that port type shall be restricted to values of the bound address type.

requirements.subject: ent:dot-notation
requirements.condition: several address types exist within a test suite
requirements.canonical: If several address types exist within a test suite, ambiguities between them SHALL be resolved by means of the dot notation.
requirements.original: If several address types exist within a test suite, ambiguities shall be resolved by means of the dot notation.

requirements.subject: ent:address-type
requirements.canonical: A reference to an address type in a variable definition used to store an SUT address MAY be prefixed by a port type identifier or a module identifier.
requirements.original: For example, a type reference within a variable definition used to store an SUT address may be prefixed by a port type identifier or a module identifier.

requirements.subject: ent:address-type
requirements.condition: both a global address type definition and port type definitions with an address declaration exist in a module
requirements.canonical: If both a global `address` type definition and port type definitions with an address declaration exist in a module, the global address type SHALL only apply to ports whose port type has no explicit address declaration.
requirements.original: If both a global address type definition and port definitions with an address type definition exist in a module, the global address type shall only affect ports without an explicit address type definition.

ambiguity.issue: 'port definitions' is used where port type definitions are meant.

requirements.subject: ent:test-suite
requirements.canonical: A test suite SHOULD consistently use explicit address declarations in port type definitions rather than a global `address` type definition.
requirements.original: The consistent use of explicit address type definitions within port definitions is recommended over the use of global address type definitions.

ambiguity.issue: 'port definitions' is used where port type definitions are meant.

requirements.subject: ent:sut-address
requirements.canonical: An explicit SUT address value of the global `address` type SHALL only be generated inside a TTCN-3 module if the `address` type is defined inside that module.
requirements.original: Explicit SUT addresses for a globally defined address type shall only be generated inside a TTCN-3 module if the type is defined inside the module itself.

requirements.subject: ent:sut-address
requirements.condition: the global address type is not defined inside the module
requirements.canonical: If the global `address` type is not defined inside the module, an explicit SUT address SHALL only be passed in as a parameter, received in a message field, or received as a parameter of a remote procedure call.
requirements.original: If the type is not defined inside the module, explicit SUT addresses for a global address type shall only be passed in as parameters or be received in message fields or as parameters of remote procedure calls.

requirements.subject: ent:null-value
requirements.canonical: The special value `null` MAY be used as a value of the address type to indicate an undefined address, e.g. for initializing variables of the address type.
requirements.original: In addition, the special value null is available for the address type to indicate an undefined address, e.g. for the initialization of variables of the address type.

requirements.subject: ent:sut-address
requirements.condition: the port type definition declares an address type
