requirements.canonical: If a port type definition declares an address type, only values of that address type SHALL be used in the `to`, `from` and `sender` parts of `receive` and `send` operations of port instances of that port type mapped to the test system interface.
requirements.original: If a port type definition includes the declaration of a type that shall be used for addressing SUT entities, only values of that type shall be used in to, from and sender parts of receive and send operations of port instances of that type mapped to the test system interface.

requirements.subject: ent:template-instance
requirements.canonical: A TemplateInstance used for addressing SHALL be of type `address` or of the address type declared in the port type definition.
requirements.original: TemplateInstance shall be of type address or of the type of the address declaration in a port type definition.

requirements.subject: ent:template-instance
requirements.condition: the TemplateInstance is of type address
requirements.canonical: If a TemplateInstance used for addressing is of type `address`, it MAY be an address type value, an address type variable or another expression of the address type.
requirements.original: If TemplateInstance is of type address, it may be an address type value, an address type variable, etc.

requirements.subject: ent:address-type
requirements.canonical: For addressing purposes, the address type SHALL only be used in the `to`, `from` and `sender` parts of communication operations of ports mapped to the test system interface.
requirements.original: b) For addressing purposes, the address type shall only be used in the to, from and sender parts of receive and send operations of ports mapped to the test system interface.

ambiguity.issue: Only 'receive and send operations' are named; procedure-based operations (call, getcall, reply, raise, ...) also have to/from/sender parts. The chosen reading treats receive and send as representatives of all communication operations.
readings: For addressing purposes, the address type SHALL only be used in the `to`, `from` and `sender` parts of communication operations of ports mapped to the test system interface.

For addressing purposes, the address type SHALL only be used in the `to`, `from` and `sender` parts of `receive` and `send` operations, and in no other operation, of ports mapped to the test system interface.

requirements.subject: ent:address-type
requirements.canonical: The address type SHALL NOT be used in the `to`, `from` and `sender` parts of `receive` and `send` operations of connected ports, i.e. ports used for communication among test components.
requirements.original: c) The address type shall not be used in the to, from and sender parts of receive and send operations of connected ports, i.e. ports used for the communication among test components.

requirements.subject: ent:structured-type
requirements.canonical: A structured type MAY be subtyped as given in table 3.
requirements.original: TTCN-3 allows subtyping of structured types as given in table 3.

requirements.subject: ent:subtype
requirements.canonical: A value of a subtype SHALL fulfil the constraint of the subtype and all constraints of all its direct and indirect parent types up to the core type.
requirements.original: Values of a subtype shall fulfil conditions specified by its constraint and all constraints existing in all its direct and indirect parent types up to the core type.

requirements.subject: ent:record-of-type
requirements.canonical: The number of elements of a value of a record of or set of type MAY be constrained.
requirements.original: TTCN-3 permits constraining the number of elements in instances of record of and set of types.

requirements.subject: ent:length-restriction
requirements.canonical: A length restriction of a record of or set of type IS written as the `length` keyword followed by a single value or a range with inclusive boundaries in parentheses, placed between the `record` or `set` keyword and the `of` keyword.
requirements.original: The length keyword followed by a value or a range (with inclusive boundaries only) within brackets and used between the record or set and the of keywords, restricts the allowed number of elements for the given record of or set of type.

ambiguity.issue: 'brackets' is used for the parentheses enclosing the length value or range.

requirements.subject: ent:length-restriction
requirements.canonical: A length restriction of a record of or set of type IS restricting the allowed number of elements of values of that type to the given value or range.
requirements.original: The length keyword followed by a value or a range (with inclusive boundaries only) within brackets and used between the record or set and the of keywords, restricts the allowed number of elements for the given record of or set of type.

requirements.subject: ent:length-restriction
requirements.canonical: The value or the bounds of a length restriction of a record of or set of type SHALL be non-negative integer values, except for an upper bound given as `infinity`.
requirements.original: The value or the bounds within the brackets shall be non-negative integer values, except when the infinity keyword is used at the place of the upper bound, in which case the maximum number of the elements is not constrained.

requirements.subject: ent:infinity-keyword
requirements.canonical: The `infinity` keyword MAY be used as the upper bound of a length restriction range of a record of or set of type.
requirements.original: The value or the bounds within the brackets shall be non-negative integer values, except when the infinity keyword is used at the place of the upper bound, in which case the maximum number of the elements is not constrained.

requirements.subject: ent:length-restriction
requirements.condition: the upper bound is infinity
requirements.canonical: If `infinity` is used as the upper bound of a length restriction, the maximum number of elements IS NOT constrained.
requirements.original: The value or the bounds within the brackets shall be non-negative integer values, except when the infinity keyword is used at the place of the upper bound, in which case the maximum number of the elements is not constrained.

requirements.subject: ent:length-restriction
requirements.canonical: The upper bound of a length restriction range SHALL NOT be less than the lower bound.
requirements.original: In case of the range syntax the upper bound shall not be lesser than the lower bound value.

requirements.subject: ent:record-of-type
requirements.canonical: A record of or set of type definition MAY be used as parent type to define a new record of or set of subtype.
requirements.original: Record of and set of type definitions may be used to define new record of or set of subtypes.

requirements.subject: ent:length-restriction
requirements.canonical: When a new record of or set of subtype is defined from a referenced record of or set of type, the `length` keyword and the value or range SHALL be placed following the identifier of the new type.
requirements.original: In this case the rules of the previous paragraph apply, except that the length keyword and the value or range defining the allowed number of iterations (within brackets) shall be placed following the identifier of the new type.

requirements.subject: ent:length-restriction
requirements.canonical: The rules on the value and bounds of a length restriction (non-negative integers, `infinity` upper bound, upper bound not less than lower bound) SHALL also apply to length subtyping of referenced record of and set of types.
requirements.original: In this case the rules of the previous paragraph apply, except that the length keyword and the value or range defining the allowed number of iterations (within brackets) shall be placed following the identifier of the new type.

requirements.subject: ent:constant
requirements.canonical: A constant used in a constant expression of length subtyping SHALL meet the restrictions of clause 10.
requirements.original: Constants used in the constant expressions of length subtyping shall meet with the restrictions in clause 10.

requirements.subject: ent:list-subtyping
requirements.canonical: List subtyping MAY be used when defining a new type based on an existing parent type.
requirements.original: List subtyping is possible when defining a new type based on an existing parent type, but not directly at the declaration of the core type (see table 3).

requirements.subject: ent:list-subtyping
requirements.canonical: List subtyping SHALL NOT be applied directly at the declaration of a core type.
requirements.original: List subtyping is possible when defining a new type based on an existing parent type, but not directly at the declaration of the core type (see table 3).

requirements.subject: ent:list-subtyping
requirements.canonical: A subtype defined by list subtyping IS restricting its allowed values to the values matched by at least one of the constraints in the list.
requirements.original: Subtypes defined by a list subtyping restrict the allowed values of the subtype to the values matched by at least one of the constraints in the list.

requirements.subject: ent:list-subtyping
requirements.canonical: In list subtyping of record, set, record of, set of, union, map and anytype types and of arrays, the list MAY contain both subtypes and possibly partial templates of the core type.
requirements.original: In case of list subtyping of `record`, `set`, `record of`, `set of`, `union`, `map` and `anytype` types, and arrays, the list may contain both subtypes and possibly partial templates of the core type.

requirements.subject: ent:expanded-list
requirements.canonical: Subtype references in a subtyping list SHALL be resolved recursively, so that the templates denoted by the referenced subtypes become members of an expanded list containing only possibly partial templates.
requirements.original: Subtype references shall be resolved in a recursive way: the collection of templates denoted by the subtype(s) referenced in the list become members of the new subtype definition with an expanded list containing only possibly partial templates.

requirements.subject: ent:expanded-list
requirements.canonical: Every value present in the expanded list of a list subtype SHALL be a valid value of the parent type.
requirements.original: All values present in the expanded list shall be valid values of the parent type.

requirements.subject: ent:partial-template
requirements.canonical: For partial values in the expanded list of a list subtype, the rules on templates given in the following sentences of this clause SHALL apply.
requirements.original: For partial (i.e. incomplete) values, all following rules on templates apply.

ambiguity.issue: 'all following rules on templates' can refer to the rules stated next in this clause or to the general template rules of clause 15; the first reading is chosen because of the word 'following'.
readings: For partial values in the expanded list of a list subtype, the rules on templates given in the following sentences of this clause SHALL apply.
For partial values in the expanded list of a list subtype, all rules on templates of the core language (clause 15) SHALL apply.

requirements.subject: ent:expanded-list
requirements.canonical: When constraining record of, set of, union, map and anytype types and arrays, every template of the expanded list SHALL be a complete value or complete template of the core type.
requirements.original: When constraining `record of`, `set of`, `union`, `map` and `anytype` types, and arrays, all templates of the expanded list (i.e. after resolving the subtype references) shall be valid (i.e. complete) values and templates of the core type.

ambiguity.issue: 'valid (i.e. complete) values and templates' leaves open whether matching mechanisms are allowed or only specific values; the reading allowing complete templates is chosen.
readings: When constraining record of, set of, union, map and anytype types and arrays, every template of the expanded list SHALL be a complete value or complete template of the core type.
When constraining record of, set of, union, map and anytype types and arrays, every element of the expanded list SHALL be a complete specific value of the core type.

requirements.subject: ent:value-list-notation
requirements.canonical: When constraining record and set types, a template of the expanded list defined using value list notation SHALL be a complete template of the core type.
requirements.original: When constraining `record` and `set` types, templates of the expanded list defined using the value list notation shall be valid (i.e. complete) templates of the core type, while templates of the expanded list defined using the field assignment notation may be partial (i.e. incomplete) templates of the core type.

requirements.subject: ent:assignment-notation
requirements.canonical: When constraining record and set types, a template of the expanded list defined using assignment notation MAY be a partial template of the core type.
requirements.original: When constraining `record` and `set` types, templates of the expanded list defined using the value list notation shall be valid (i.e. complete) templates of the core type, while templates of the expanded list defined using the field assignment notation may be partial (i.e. incomplete) templates of the core type.

ambiguity.issue: 'field assignment notation' is used instead of the glossary term 'assignment notation'.

requirements.subject: ent:partial-template
requirements.canonical: In a partial template defined with assignment notation in the expanded list of a record or set list subtype, a field that is not explicitly present SHALL be considered as containing AnyValue if it is mandatory and AnyValueOrNone if it is optional.
requirements.original: In the latter case, the fields that are not explicitly present shall be considered as containing AnyValue for mandatory fields and _AnyValueOrNone_ for optional fields.

requirements.subject: ent:ttcn3-user
requirements.canonical: A TTCN-3 user SHOULD assign new values to single fields of values or templates of list-subtyped record or set types cautiously.
requirements.original: > NOTE: Users should assign new values to single fields of values/templates based on types using list subtyping cautiously: it may happen that the new field value would be valid with other combination(s) of the rest of the fields but causes an erroneous record/set value, when combining with the actual values of the other fields.

requirements.subject: ent:list-subtyping
requirements.canonical: Assigning a new value to a single field of a value of a list-subtyped record or set type CAN cause an erroneous value when the new field value is not allowed in combination with the actual values of the other fields.
requirements.original: > NOTE: Users should assign new values to single fields of values/templates based on types using list subtyping cautiously: it may happen that the new field value would be valid with other combination(s) of the rest of the fields but causes an erroneous record/set value, when combining with the actual values of the other fields.

requirements.subject: ent:enumerated-type
requirements.canonical: A list subtype of an enumerated type SHALL contain only values of the parent type.
requirements.original: In case of `enumerated` types, the template list subtyping shall contain only values of the parent type.

ambiguity.issue: 'template list subtyping' is used instead of 'list subtyping'.

requirements.subject: ent:innermost-type
requirements.canonical: A type restriction following the identifier of a newly defined record of or set of type (defined with the `record of` or `set of` keywords) SHALL constrain the innermost type.
requirements.original: A type restriction following the identifier of a newly defined record of or set of type (i.e. when the keywords record and of or set and of are used in the definition) shall constrain the innermost type.

requirements.subject: ent:innermost-type
requirements.canonical: The iterated type of a newly defined record of or set of type with a type restriction SHALL be a subset of the innermost type.
requirements.original: The newly defined iterated type shall be a subset of the innermost type.

requirements.subject: ent:innermost-type
requirements.condition: the innermost type is a basic type
requirements.canonical: If the innermost type of a record of or set of type is a basic type, the subtyping rules of clause 6.1.2 SHALL apply to the type restriction.
requirements.original: If the innermost type is a basic type, the subtyping rules in clause 6.1.2 shall apply.

requirements.subject: ent:innermost-type
requirements.condition: the innermost type references a structured type or anytype
requirements.canonical: If the innermost type of a record of or set of type references a structured type or anytype, the rules of clauses 6.2.13.1 and 6.2.13.2 SHALL apply to the type restriction.
requirements.original: If the innermost type is referencing a structured type or anytype, the rules in clauses 6.2.13.1 and 6.2.13.2 shall apply.

requirements.subject: ent:subtyping-mechanism
requirements.canonical: A subtype definition of a structured type or anytype SHALL NOT mix different subtyping mechanisms (e.g. list and length subtyping).
requirements.original: In the case of structured types and the special type anytype, it is forbidden to mix different subtyping mechanisms (e.g. list and length) in the same definition.

requirements.subject: ent:timer-type
requirements.canonical: Constants, variables and formal parameters of timer type MAY be defined.
requirements.original: TTCN-3 allows to define timer constants, variables and parameters.

ambiguity.issue: 'parameters' is used where formal parameters are meant.

requirements.subject: ent:timer-reference
requirements.canonical: A constant, variable or formal parameter of timer type CAN contain a reference to an existing timer or the special value `null`.
requirements.original: These constants, variables or parameters can contain a reference to an existing timer or a special value null.

requirements.subject: ent:null-value
requirements.canonical: The special value `null` of timer type IS an unspecified timer reference.
requirements.original: The special value null represents an unspecified timer reference, i.e. can be used for variables to explicitly reference no timer.

requirements.subject: ent:null-value
requirements.canonical: The special value `null` MAY be assigned to a timer variable to explicitly reference no timer.
requirements.original: The special value null represents an unspecified timer reference, i.e. can be used for variables to explicitly reference no timer.

requirements.subject: ent:timer-reference
requirements.canonical: A timer reference IS meaningful only within the test component instance where the timer is defined.
requirements.original: Timer references have meaning only within the test component instances where the timer is defined, i.e. a timer reference assigned to a timer variable in a test component instance "a1" of type "A" has no meaning in a test component instance "a2" of type "A".

ambiguity.issue: The consequence of using a timer reference in another test component instance (error, or unspecified behaviour) is not stated.
readings: Using a timer reference in a test component instance other than the one where the timer is defined causes a dynamic error.
Using a timer reference in a test component instance other than the one where the timer is defined has unspecified behaviour.

requirements.subject: ent:timer-type
requirements.canonical: A value of timer type IS an object reference and follows the rules for object references.
requirements.original: The values of timer type are object references and follow specific rules for this kind of values.

requirements.subject: ent:map-type
requirements.canonical: A map type IS a type that maps a set of unique keys to a set of values such that each key is associated with exactly one value.
requirements.original: TTCN-3 supports the specification of map types that map from a set of unique keys to a set of values in such a way that each value in the set of key is associated with exactly one value in the set of values.

ambiguity.issue: The sentence says 'each value in the set of key is associated with exactly one value'; the intended meaning is 'each key in the set of keys'.

improper_terms.used: each value in the set of key
improper_terms.proper: each key in the set of keys

requirements.subject: ent:map-key
requirements.canonical: Each key of a map type value IS associated with exactly one value.
requirements.original: TTCN-3 supports the specification of map types that map from a set of unique keys to a set of values in such a way that each value in the set of key is associated with exactly one value in the set of values.

requirements.subject: ent:map-type
requirements.canonical: A map type definition has the syntax `type map from` Type `to` Type Identifier.
requirements.original: **type** **map** **from** _Type_ **to** _Type_ _Identifier_

requirements.subject: ent:map-key-type
requirements.canonical: The Type following the `from` keyword in a map type definition IS the key type of the map type.
requirements.original: The Type following the from keyword is the type of the keys of the map type.

requirements.subject: ent:map-value-type
requirements.canonical: The Type following the `to` keyword in a map type definition IS the value type of the map type.
requirements.original: The Type following the to keyword is the type of the values of the map type.

requirements.subject: ent:index-assignment-notation
requirements.canonical: A map value or template in index assignment notation has the syntax "{" ["*" ","] { "[" Index "]" ":=" Value "," } "}".

requirements.subject: ent:map-value
requirements.canonical: A map value MAY be denoted with the index assignment notation.
requirements.original: Values of the map type can be denoted with the indexed assignment notation where the indices are values of the key type of the map type and the right hand sides are values of the value type.

ambiguity.issue: The text says 'indexed assignment notation' while the restriction of the same clause and clause 6.2.15.4 use 'index assignment notation'.

requirements.subject: ent:index-expression
requirements.canonical: An index in the index assignment notation of a map value SHALL be a value of the key type of the map type.
requirements.original: Values of the map type can be denoted with the indexed assignment notation where the indices are values of the key type of the map type and the right hand sides are values of the value type.

requirements.subject: ent:value
requirements.canonical: The right hand side of an indexed assignment in the index assignment notation of a map value SHALL be a value of the value type of the map type.
requirements.original: Values of the map type can be denoted with the indexed assignment notation where the indices are values of the key type of the map type and the right hand sides are values of the value type.

requirements.subject: ent:map-template
requirements.canonical: A map template MAY use a mixed notation in which the first item is an asterisk representing the AnyElementsOrNone matching symbol, followed by one or more indexed assignments.
requirements.original: Templates of the map type can use a specific form of the mixed notation, where the first item is and asterisk representing the AnyElementsOrNone matching symbol, followed by one or more indexed assignments (see clause B.1.3.2 for more details).

ambiguity.issue: The prose requires 'one or more' indexed assignments after the asterisk, but the syntactical structure { ... } allows zero or more. The prose reading is used in the canonical text.
readings: A map template MAY use a mixed notation consisting of an asterisk followed by one or more indexed assignments.
A map template MAY use a mixed notation consisting of an asterisk followed by zero or more indexed assignments, i.e. { * } alone is valid.

requirements.subject: ent:asterisk-literal
requirements.canonical: In the mixed notation of a map template, the asterisk representing AnyElementsOrNone SHALL be the first item.
requirements.original: Templates of the map type can use a specific form of the mixed notation, where the first item is and asterisk representing the AnyElementsOrNone matching symbol, followed by one or more indexed assignments (see clause B.1.3.2 for more details).

requirements.subject: ent:index-assignment-notation
requirements.canonical: When the index assignment notation is used on the right hand side of an assignment, each element to be changed IS identified explicitly by its key.
requirements.original: When using the indexed assignment notation on the right hand side of an assignment, elements for keys to be changed are identified explicitly and either a value or the not used symbol "-" can be assigned to them.

requirements.subject: ent:not-used-symbol
requirements.canonical: In the index assignment notation on the right hand side of an assignment, either a value or the not used symbol "-" MAY be assigned to an element identified by a key.
requirements.original: When using the indexed assignment notation on the right hand side of an assignment, elements for keys to be changed are identified explicitly and either a value or the not used symbol "-" can be assigned to them.

requirements.subject: ent:map-value
requirements.condition: the index assignment notation is used on the right hand side of an assignment
requirements.canonical: When the index assignment notation is assigned to a map variable, elements whose keys are not referred to in the notation SHALL remain unchanged.
requirements.original: Other elements, not referred to by keys in the notation, shall remain unchanged.

requirements.subject: ent:not-used-symbol
requirements.canonical: Re-assigning a previously initialized element using the not used symbol or by skipping it in an assignment notation leaves that element unchanged.
requirements.original: Re-assigning a previously initialized value, using the not used symbol or just skipping a field or element in an assignment notation, will cause that field or element to remain unchanged.

requirements.subject: ent:index-expression
requirements.canonical: In the index assignment notation, every index expression SHALL evaluate to a value different from all other index expressions of the same notation.
requirements.original: a) In the index assignment notation, every index expression shall evaluate to a different value than all the other ones.

requirements.subject: ent:unmap-statement
requirements.canonical: The unmap statement has the syntax `unmap` "(" ValueRef "," [SingleExpression | "*"] ")".
requirements.original: **unmap "(" ValueRef "," [ SingleExpression | "*"] ")"**

requirements.subject: ent:unmap-statement
requirements.canonical: The `unmap` statement MAY be used to remove the mapping of a key to its associated value from a variable of a map type.
requirements.original: To remove a mapping from a key to its associated value in a variable of a map type, the unmap statement may be used.

ambiguity.issue: Clause 6.2.15.3 calls it 'unmap statement' while the next sentences and the NOTE in 6.2.15.9 call it 'unmap operation'; 'unmap operation' also names the port unmap operation.

requirements.subject: ent:unmap-statement
requirements.condition: the map variable did not associate the given key with a value
requirements.canonical: If the map variable does not associate the given key with a value, the `unmap` statement has no effect.
requirements.original: If the map variable did not associate the given key with a value, the operation has no effect.

requirements.subject: ent:unmap-statement
requirements.canonical: The `unmap` statement MAY be used to remove the AnyElementsOrNone matching symbol from a map template variable.
requirements.original: The unmap statement may be also used to remove the AnyElementsOrNone matching symbol from a map template variable.

requirements.subject: ent:asterisk-literal
requirements.condition: unmap is used to remove AnyElementsOrNone from a map template variable
requirements.canonical: When the `unmap` statement is used to remove AnyElementsOrNone from a map template variable, its second parameter SHALL be an asterisk literal.
requirements.original: In this case, the second parameter of the statement shall be an asterisk literal.

requirements.subject: ent:unmap-statement
requirements.condition: the template variable does not contain AnyElementsOrNone
requirements.canonical: If the map template variable does not contain the AnyElementsOrNone matching symbol, `unmap` with an asterisk as second parameter has no effect.
requirements.original: If the template variable does not contain the AnyElementsOrNone matching symbol, the operation has no effect.

requirements.subject: ent:unmap-statement
requirements.canonical: The ValueRef of an `unmap` statement SHALL be an initialized variable (or template variable) of a map type.
requirements.original: a) ValueRef shall be an initialized variable of map type and SingleExpression shall be a value compatible with the key type of the map type of ValueRef.

ambiguity.issue: The restriction says 'variable of map type', but the semantic description also allows map template variables; it is unclear whether a template variable satisfies the restriction. The reading that includes template variables is used.
readings: The ValueRef of an unmap statement SHALL be an initialized variable or template variable of a map type.
The ValueRef of an unmap statement SHALL be an initialized (value) variable of a map type; template variables are only allowed with the asterisk form.

requirements.subject: ent:index-expression
requirements.canonical: The SingleExpression of an `unmap` statement SHALL be a value compatible with the key type of the map type of the ValueRef.
requirements.original: a) ValueRef shall be an initialized variable of map type and SingleExpression shall be a value compatible with the key type of the map type of ValueRef.

requirements.subject: ent:index-notation
requirements.canonical: The index notation on a map value or template has the syntax ValueRef "[" (Index | "*") "]".
requirements.original: _ValueRef_ "[" Index | "*" "]"

requirements.subject: ent:index-notation
requirements.canonical: The index notation on a map MAY be used on both the right hand side and the left hand side of an assignment.
requirements.original: Index notation can be used on both the right-hand side and left-hand side of assignments.

requirements.subject: ent:index-notation
requirements.canonical: The index notation with a key used on the right hand side refers to the value element that the map value or template associates with that key.
requirements.original: The index notation, when used on the right-hand side, refers to the value element that the map value or template associates with the key given as the index or with the presence of the AnyElementsOrNone matching symbol if asterisk is used instead of the index.

requirements.subject: ent:index-notation
requirements.canonical: The index notation with an asterisk instead of an index used on the right hand side refers to the presence of the AnyElementsOrNone matching symbol in the map template.
requirements.original: The index notation, when used on the right-hand side, refers to the value element that the map value or template associates with the key given as the index or with the presence of the AnyElementsOrNone matching symbol if asterisk is used instead of the index.

requirements.subject: ent:index-notation
requirements.condition: a key is used as index
requirements.canonical: When the index notation with a key is used on the left hand side of an assignment, only the value associated with that key is changed and values with other keys remain unchanged.
requirements.original: When the index notation is used at the left-hand side, only the value associated with the index key is changed, values with other keys remain unchanged.

requirements.subject: ent:index-notation
requirements.canonical: Assigning to the index notation with a key that already has an associated value causes the key to be mapped to the newly assigned value.
requirements.original: Using the index notation on the left hand side of an assignment with a key that already has a value associated with it causes the key to be mapped to the newly assigned value.

requirements.subject: ent:fn-isbound
requirements.canonical: The presence of a mapping for a key MAY be checked by using the `isbound`, `isvalue` or `ispresent` operation with an index notation as its argument.
requirements.original: Presence of a mapping for a key can be checked by using the isbound, isvalue or ispresent operation with an index notation as its argument.

requirements.subject: ent:index-notation
requirements.condition: the asterisk is used instead of an index
requirements.canonical: When the index notation with an asterisk is used on the left hand side of an assignment, only the presence of AnyElementsOrNone in the map template is changed and values and keys remain unchanged.
requirements.original: When the asterisk symbol is used at the left-hand side of an assignment, only the presence of the AnyElementsOrNone within the template is changed, values and keys remain unchanged.

requirements.subject: ent:assignment
requirements.condition: the asterisk index notation is on the left hand side
requirements.canonical: When the index notation with an asterisk is used on the left hand side of an assignment, the right hand side of the assignment SHALL resolve into a boolean value.
requirements.original: The right-hand side of the assignment shall resolve into a boolean value in this case.

requirements.subject: ent:index-notation
requirements.canonical: When the index notation with an asterisk is used on the right hand side of an assignment, it returns a boolean value indicating whether AnyElementsOrNone is present in the map template.
requirements.original: When used at the right-hand side of an assignment, the notation returns a boolean value indicating if the _AnyElementsOrNone_ is present within the map template.

requirements.subject: ent:fn-isbound
requirements.canonical: The presence of AnyElementsOrNone in a map template MAY be checked by using the `isbound` or `ispresent` operation with an index notation containing the asterisk as its argument.
requirements.original: Presence of the AnyElementsOrNone in a map template can be checked by using the isbound or ispresent operation with an index notation containing the asterisk symbol as its argument.

requirements.subject: ent:index-expression
requirements.canonical: The index expression used in the index notation and in the index assignment notation of a map SHALL be completely initialized.
requirements.original: a) The index expression used for index notation and index assignment notation shall be completely initialized and compatible with the from type of the map type.

requirements.subject: ent:index-expression
requirements.canonical: The index expression used in the index notation and in the index assignment notation of a map SHALL be compatible with the key (`from`) type of the map type.
requirements.original: a) The index expression used for index notation and index assignment notation shall be completely initialized and compatible with the from type of the map type.

requirements.subject: ent:value
requirements.canonical: When the index notation of a map value with a key is used as the left hand side of an assignment, the assigned value SHALL be compatible with the value (`to`) type of the map type.
requirements.original: b) When an index operation of a map value with a key as an index is used as the left-hand side of an assignment, the assigned value shall be compatible with the to type of the map type.

requirements.subject: ent:index-notation
requirements.canonical: The index notation used on the right hand side with a key that has no associated value SHALL result in a test case error.
requirements.original: c) An index notation used on the right hand side with a key that has no associated value shall result in an error.

ambiguity.issue: The restriction says 'an error'; the example clarifies that a test case error (runtime) is meant.

requirements.subject: ent:from-selector
requirements.canonical: The set of keys that a map associates with a value MAY be accessed using the `from` selector.
requirements.original: The set of keys that the map associates with a value can be accessed using the from selector.

requirements.subject: ent:from-selector
requirements.canonical: The `from` selector on a map value has the syntax MapValue "." `from`.
requirements.original: _MapValue "." from_

requirements.subject: ent:from-selector
requirements.canonical: The `from` selector on a map type has the syntax MapValueType "." `from`.
requirements.original: _MapValueType_ "." `from`

requirements.subject: ent:from-selector
requirements.canonical: If MapValue is a value of a type defined as `map from` A `to` B, then MapValue.from yields a result compatible with type `set of` A that contains all key values of MapValue.
requirements.original: If the MapValue is a value of type MapValueType defined as map from _A_ to _B_ then MapValue.from yields a result compatible with type set of A that contains all the key values from MapValue.

requirements.subject: ent:from-selector
requirements.canonical: The type `set of` A of the key set of a map type MapValueType defined as `map from` A `to` B MAY be referenced as MapValueType.from.
requirements.original: This type can also be referenced as _MapValueType.from._

requirements.subject: ent:map-value
requirements.canonical: In a map value, exactly one value IS mapped to each key.
requirements.original: There is always exactly one value mapped to each key in a map value.

requirements.subject: ent:map-key
requirements.canonical: Each value in the set of keys of a map value IS unique.
requirements.original: The values in the set of keys are always unique, so comparing two values from the set of keys that have a different index using the equality operator will always yield false.

requirements.subject: ent:equality-operator
requirements.canonical: Comparing two elements with different indices of the set of keys of a map value using the equality operator IS always false.
requirements.original: The values in the set of keys are always unique, so comparing two values from the set of keys that have a different index using the equality operator will always yield false.

requirements.subject: ent:from-selector
requirements.canonical: The length of the set of keys of a map value IS equal to the length of the map value, i.e. the number of key value pairs.
requirements.original: Since the length of the map value is equal to the number of key value pairs in the map value and there is precisely one key per value, the length of the set of keys is equal to the length of the map value.

requirements.subject: ent:from-selector
requirements.canonical: The order in which the keys of a map type value are enumerated IS NOT specified.
requirements.original: NOTE: It is unspecified in which order the keys of a map type value are enumerated.

requirements.subject: ent:to-selector
requirements.canonical: The set of values that a map contains MAY be accessed using the `to` selector.
requirements.original: The set of values that the map contains can be accessed using the to selector.

requirements.subject: ent:to-selector
requirements.canonical: The `to` selector on a map value has the syntax MapValue "." `to`.
requirements.original: MapValue "." to

requirements.subject: ent:to-selector
requirements.canonical: The `to` selector on a map type has the syntax MapValueType "." `to`.
requirements.original: MapValueType "." `to`

requirements.subject: ent:to-selector
requirements.canonical: If MapValue is a value of a type defined as `map from` A `to` B, then MapValue.to yields a result compatible with type `set of` B that contains all values of MapValue.
requirements.original: If MapValue is a value of type MapValueType defined as map `from` _A_ `to` _B then MapValue.to yields a result_ compatible with type set of _B that contains all the values from MapValue.

requirements.subject: ent:to-selector
requirements.canonical: The type `set of` B of the value set of a map type MapValueType defined as `map from` A `to` B MAY be referenced as MapValueType.to.
requirements.original: This type can also be referenced as_ _MapValueType.to;_

requirements.subject: ent:to-selector
requirements.canonical: The set of values of a map value CAN contain duplicate values, because two different keys can be mapped to the same value.
requirements.original: Since two different keys might be mapped to the same value in a map value, the values in the set of values might not be unique.

requirements.subject: ent:to-selector
requirements.canonical: The set of values of a map value IS composed of exactly one value for each key value pair in the map.
requirements.original: The set of values will contain one value for each key value pair in the map.

requirements.subject: ent:to-selector
requirements.canonical: The length of the set of values of a map value IS equal to the length of the map value, i.e. the number of key value pairs.
requirements.original: Since the length of the map value is equal to number of key value pairs in the map value and there is precisely one item for each key value pair in the set of values, the length of the set of values is equal to the length of map value.

requirements.subject: ent:to-selector
requirements.canonical: The order in which the values of a map type value are enumerated IS NOT specified.
requirements.original: NOTE: It is unspecified in which order the values of a map type value are enumerated.

requirements.subject: ent:reference-expansion
requirements.condition: an element of an uninitialized map value, field or omitted field is referenced on the left hand side of an assignment
requirements.canonical: When an element of an uninitialized or omitted map value or field is referenced on the left hand side of an assignment, the reference SHALL be recursively expanded up to and including the depth of the referenced element.
requirements.original: When referencing an element of an uninitialized map value or field or omitted field (including omitting a field at a higher level of the embedding hierarchy) on the left-hand side of an assignment, the reference shall recursively be expanded up to and including the depth of the referenced element as follows:

requirements.subject: ent:reference-expansion
requirements.canonical: When a value or value field of map type is expanded, the element referenced by the index notation SHALL be set to present.
requirements.original: a) When expanding a value or value field of map type, the element referenced by the index notation shall be set to present.

requirements.subject: ent:reference-expansion
requirements.canonical: During expansion of a map reference, expansion of record, record of, set of, union and set values and intermediate fields SHALL follow item a) of clauses 6.2.1.1, 6.2.3.0, 6.2.5.1 and 6.2.2.1 respectively.
requirements.original: b) Expansion of record, record of and set of, union and set values and intermediate fields shall follow the rules of item a) in clauses 6.2.1.1, 6.2.3.0 and 6.2.5.1 and clause 6.2.2.1 correspondingly.

requirements.subject: ent:assignment
requirements.canonical: At the end of the expansion, the value on the right hand side of the assignment SHALL be assigned to the referenced element.
requirements.original: c) At the end of the expansion, the value at the right-hand side of the assignment shall be assigned to the referenced element.

requirements.subject: ent:map-value-type
requirements.canonical: A map type MAY have a nested structured type as its value (`to`) type.
requirements.original: TTCN-3 supports the definition of map types with nested structured types for the to part.

requirements.subject: ent:map-value-type
requirements.canonical: The value (`to`) type of a map type MAY be a record, set, enumerated, set of, record of, union or map type.
requirements.original: The usage of structured types (record, set, enumerated, set `of, record` `of, union and map) is allowed.`

ambiguity.issue: It is unclear whether the permission of structured types applies only to the 'to' part (as the preceding sentence says) or also to the key type (the NOTE implies structured keys are allowed but discouraged). The 'to'-only reading is used here.
readings: The value (to) type of a map type MAY be a structured type.
Both the key (from) type and the value (to) type of a map type MAY be structured types.

requirements.subject: ent:map-key-type
requirements.canonical: The key type of a map type SHOULD be a basic type.
requirements.original: NOTE: It is recommended that only basic types are used for the keys of map types.

requirements.subject: ent:map-key-type
requirements.canonical: Using complex structured types as key type of a map type CAN have a negative impact on the speed of execution.
requirements.original: Using complex structured types for keys of map types can have negative impact on the speed of the execution.

requirements.subject: ent:map-value
requirements.canonical: In a map value, each key and its associated value field IS mandatory.
requirements.original: In map values, both keys and value fields associated with them are mandatory.

requirements.subject: ent:omit-symbol
requirements.canonical: The `omit` symbol SHALL NOT be assigned to a map key or to a map value field.
requirements.original: The omit symbol shall not be assigned to a map key or value field.

requirements.subject: ent:unmap-statement
requirements.canonical: A key IS removed from a map by the `unmap` operation (not by assigning `omit`).
requirements.original: NOTE: The unmap operation is used for removing a key from a map.

ambiguity.issue: The NOTE calls it 'unmap operation' while clause 6.2.15.3 calls it 'unmap statement'; 'unmap operation' also denotes the port unmap operation.

requirements.subject: ent:map-key
requirements.canonical: A key of a map template SHALL NOT contain matching symbols.
requirements.original: Keys of map templates shall not contain matching symbols.

requirements.subject: ent:map-template
requirements.canonical: A value field associated with a key of a map template MAY contain matching symbols, including `omit`, `*` and `ifpresent`.
requirements.original: Value fields associated with keys of map templates might contain matching symbols including symbols for optional fields such as omit, * or ifpresent (see Annex B for more details).

ambiguity.issue: 6.2.15.9-s002 forbids assigning omit to a map value field, while this sentence allows omit, * and ifpresent in map template value fields; also 'might' can be read as permission or as possibility. The permission reading for templates is used.
readings: A value field of a map template MAY contain omit, * or ifpresent.
A value field of a map template MAY contain matching symbols, but omit (and therefore * / ifpresent with omit semantics) is excluded by the prohibition of omit for map value fields.

requirements.subject: ent:open-type
requirements.canonical: The open type IS represented by the keyword `any`.
requirements.original: The open type is represented by the keyword any.

requirements.subject: ent:actual-parameter
requirements.canonical: A value of any type MAY be passed directly as an actual parameter to a formal parameter of the open type without explicitly specifying a type context.
requirements.original: Values of all types can be directly passed as actual parameters to formal parameters of the open type without the need to explicitly specify a type context.

requirements.subject: ent:open-type
requirements.canonical: The open type SHALL only be used as the type of a formal parameter of a predefined or external function.
requirements.original: a) The open type shall be used only in formal parameter of predefined or external functions.

requirements.subject: ent:open-type
requirements.canonical: The open type SHALL NOT be used in a type declaration.
requirements.original: Type declarations

requirements.subject: ent:open-type
requirements.canonical: The open type SHALL NOT be used in a variable declaration.
requirements.original: Variable declarations

requirements.subject: ent:open-type
requirements.canonical: The open type SHALL NOT be used in a template declaration.
requirements.original: Template declarations

requirements.subject: ent:open-type
requirements.canonical: The open type SHALL NOT be used in a constant declaration.
requirements.original: Constant declarations

requirements.subject: ent:open-type
requirements.canonical: The open type SHALL NOT be used in a module parameter declaration.
requirements.original: Module parameter declarations

requirements.subject: ent:open-type
requirements.canonical: The open type SHALL NOT be used as the type of a formal parameter of a template, testcase, altstep, non-external function, map operation or unmap operation.
requirements.original: Formal parameters of templates, test cases, altsteps, non-external functions, map and unmap operations

ambiguity.issue: 'map and unmap operations' may denote the port map/unmap operations (which have a param clause) or the map type unmap statement of clause 6.2.15.3. The port operation reading is used.
readings: The open type SHALL NOT be used in the param clause of the port map and unmap operations.
The open type SHALL NOT be used as an argument type of the unmap statement on map variables (clause 6.2.15.3).

requirements.subject: ent:open-type
requirements.canonical: The open type SHALL NOT be used in the return clause of a function.
requirements.original: Return clauses of functions

requirements.subject: ent:value
requirements.canonical: A value used in an assignment, an instantiation or a comparison SHALL be type compatible with the type of the target or of the other operand.
requirements.original: Generally, TTCN-3 requires type compatibility of values at assignments, instantiations and comparison.

ambiguity.issue: 'Generally' implies exceptions without listing them here; the exceptions (strong typing) are given in clause 6.3.4. Chose the reading that type compatibility is the default rule.
readings: A value used in an assignment, an instantiation or a comparison SHALL be type compatible with the target type, except where clause 6.3.4 requires strong typing.
A value used in an assignment, an instantiation or a comparison SHALL be type compatible with the target type in all cases.

requirements.subject: ent:value-b
requirements.canonical: Value "b" IS the actual value that is assigned, passed as parameter, etc., in the type compatibility rules of clause 6.3.
requirements.original: For the purpose of this clause the actual value to be assigned, passed as parameter, etc. is called value "b".

requirements.subject: ent:type-b
requirements.canonical: Type "B" IS the type of value "b" in the type compatibility rules of clause 6.3.
requirements.original: The type of value "b" is called type "B".

requirements.subject: ent:type-a
requirements.canonical: Type "A" IS the type of the object (formal parameter, variable, etc.) that obtains value "b" in the type compatibility rules of clause 6.3.
requirements.original: The type of the formal parameter, which is to obtain the actual value of value "b" is called type "A".

ambiguity.issue: Type "A" is defined only as the type of a formal parameter, but the rules of clause 6.3 also apply to assignments and comparisons. Chose the wider reading.
readings: Type "A" IS the type of the object (formal parameter, variable, etc.) that obtains value "b".
Type "A" IS only the type of the formal parameter that obtains value "b".

improper_terms.proper: target object (formal parameter, variable, template variable, field)

requirements.subject: ent:address-type
requirements.canonical: An `address` type and its derivatives ARE subject to the same type compatibility rules as a type with the same definition but a name different from `address`.
requirements.original: NOTE: As address is more a predefined type name than a distinct type with its own properties, the same type compatibility rules apply to an address type and to its derivatives as the rules were if the type was defined with a name different from address.

requirements.subject: ent:value-b
requirements.condition: type "B" is a simple basic type or basic string type
requirements.canonical: A value "b" of a simple basic type or basic string type IS compatible with type "A" if type "B" resolves to the same root type as type "A" and value "b" does not violate the subtyping (e.g. ranges, length restrictions) of type "A".
requirements.original: For variables, constants, templates, etc. of simple basic types and basic string types the value "b" is compatible to type "A" if type "B" resolves to the same root type as type "A" (e.g. integer) and it does not violate subtyping (e.g. ranges, length restrictions) of type "A".

requirements.subject: ent:charstring-type
requirements.canonical: A value "b" of charstring type IS compatible with a universal charstring type "A" unless value "b" violates a type constraint specification (range, list or length) of type "A".
requirements.original: For variables, constants, templates, etc. of charstring type, value 'b' is compatible with a universal charstring type 'A' unless it violates any type constraint specification (range, list or length) of type "A".

requirements.subject: ent:universal-charstring-type
requirements.canonical: A value "b" of universal charstring type IS compatible with a charstring type "A" if every character of value "b" has a corresponding character (the same control or graphical character with the same character code) in the charstring type and value "b" does not violate a type constraint specification (range, list or length) of type "A".
requirements.original: For variables, constants, templates, etc. of universal charstring type, value 'b' is compatible with a charstring type 'A' if all characters used in value 'b' have their corresponding characters (i.e. the same control or graphical character using the same character code) in the type charstring and it does not violate any type constraint specification (range, list or length) of type "A".

requirements.subject: ent:value-b
requirements.canonical: In clause 6.3.2, value "b" IS the value to be assigned (e.g. passed as parameter) to an object of type "A".
requirements.original: In subsequent clauses, "value "b"" is called the value to be assigned, e.g. when passed as parameter, to an object of type "A".

requirements.subject: ent:enumerated-type
requirements.canonical: An enumerated type IS NOT compatible with any type other than an enumerated type.
requirements.original: Enumerated types are only compatible with other enumerated types.

requirements.subject: ent:enumerated-value
requirements.canonical: An enumerated value "b" of an enumerated type "B" IS compatible with an enumerated type "A" if the identifier of value "b" is also defined in type "A" and the integer value(s) associated with value "b" are associated with the same identifier in type "A".
requirements.original: An enumerated value "b" of an enumerated type "B" is compatible with enumerated type "A" if the identifier of the value "b" is also defined in "A" and the integer(s) associated with value "b" are also associated with the same identifier in "A".

requirements.subject: ent:record-type
requirements.canonical: A value "b" of record type "B" IS compatible with record type "A" if the number and the optionality of the fields in textual order of definition are identical, the types of corresponding fields are compatible, and the value of each present field of value "b" is compatible with the type of the corresponding field in type "A".
requirements.original: record types are compatible if the number, and optional aspect of the fields in the textual order of definition are identical, the types of each field are compatible and the value of each existing field of the value "b" is compatible with the type of its corresponding field in type "A".

ambiguity.issue: 'the types of each field are compatible' does not say whether field types need only the same root type or must be compatible including subtyping; EXAMPLE 1 accepts AType (field a(0..10)) and BType (field a integer), so the root-type reading was chosen. Field names are irrelevant (EXAMPLE 1, CType).
readings: Corresponding field types SHALL resolve to the same root type; subtype violations are checked on the field values of value "b".
Corresponding field types SHALL be compatible including their subtype constraints.

requirements.subject: ent:value-b
requirements.canonical: When a value "b" of a record type is assigned to an object of a compatible record type "A", the value of each field of value "b" IS assigned to the positionally corresponding field of the value of type "A".
requirements.original: The value of each field in the value "b" is assigned to the corresponding field in the value of type "A".

requirements.subject: ent:record-of-type
requirements.canonical: A value "b" of a `record of` type or array type IS compatible with a `record of` type or array type "A" if the element types are compatible and value "b" does not violate any length subtyping of the `record of` type "A" or the dimensions of the array type "A".
requirements.original: `record of` types and arrays are compatible if their element types are compatible and value "b" does not violate any length subtyping of the `record of` type "A" or dimensions of the array type.

requirements.subject: ent:value-b
requirements.canonical: When a value "b" of a `record of` or array type is assigned to an instance of type "A", the element values of value "b" SHALL be assigned sequentially to the instance of type "A", including undefined elements.
requirements.original: Values of elements of the value "b" shall be assigned sequentially to the instance of type "A", including undefined elements.

requirements.subject: ent:array
requirements.canonical: An array type IS compatible with another array type if their corresponding `record of` types are compatible.
requirements.original: Two array types are compatible if their corresponding `record of` types are compatible.

requirements.subject: ent:set-type
requirements.canonical: A set type IS NOT compatible with any type other than a set type.
requirements.original: set types are only compatible with other set types and set of types are only compatible with other set of types.

requirements.subject: ent:set-of-type
requirements.canonical: A `set of` type IS NOT compatible with any type other than a `set of` type.
requirements.original: set types are only compatible with other set types and set of types are only compatible with other set of types.

requirements.subject: ent:set-type
requirements.canonical: The compatibility rules for record types SHALL apply to set types.
requirements.original: For set types the same compatibility rules shall apply as to record types and for set `of types the same` compatibility rules shall apply as to record `of types.`

requirements.subject: ent:set-of-type
requirements.canonical: The compatibility rules for `record of` types SHALL apply to `set of` types.
requirements.original: For set types the same compatibility rules shall apply as to record types and for set `of types the same` compatibility rules shall apply as to record `of types.`

requirements.subject: ent:set-type
requirements.canonical: When determining type compatibility of set types, the textual order of the fields in the set type definition IS decisive, although the order of elements at sending and receipt is unknown.
requirements.original: NOTE 1: This implies that though the order of elements at sending and receipt is unknown, when determining type compatibility for set types, the textual order of the fields in the type definition is decisive.

requirements.subject: ent:set-type
requirements.canonical: The arbitrary order of fields in a set value IS NOT relevant for type compatibility, because the field names identify which fields of the set type correspond to which set value fields.
requirements.original: NOTE 2: In set values the order of fields may be arbitrary, however this does not affect type compatibility as field names unambiguously identify, which fields of the related set type correspond to which set value fields.

requirements.subject: ent:union-value
requirements.canonical: A union value "b" of union type "B" IS compatible with union type "A" if the alternative selected in value "b" has a corresponding alternative with identical name in type "A" and the value of the selected alternative is compatible with the type of that corresponding alternative.
requirements.original: A union value "b" of union type "B" is compatible with union type "A" if the alternative selected in "b" has a corresponding alternative with identical name in "A" and the value of the selected alternative in "b" is compatible to the type of the corresponding alternative in "A".

requirements.subject: ent:union-value
requirements.condition: the first union compatibility rule did not determine compatibility
requirements.canonical: A union value "b" of union type "B" with a default alternative of type "C" IS compatible with an arbitrary type "A" if the alternative selected in value "b" is the default alternative and the value of the default alternative is compatible with type "A".
requirements.original: A union value "b" of union type "B" with a default alternative of type "C" is compatible with an arbitrary type "A" if the alternative selected in "b" is the default alternative and the value of the default alternative is compatible to "A".

requirements.subject: ent:value
requirements.condition: the first union compatibility rule did not determine compatibility
requirements.canonical: A value "a" of an arbitrary type "A" IS compatible with a union type "B" with a default alternative of type "C" if value "a" is compatible with type "C".
requirements.original: A value "a" of an arbitrary type "A" is compatible with a **union type "B" with a default alternative of type "C" if value "a" is compatible to "C".**

requirements.subject: ent:ttcn3-tool
requirements.canonical: When checking the compatibility of two union types, a TTCN-3 tool SHALL first apply the rule based on identically named alternatives, which does not depend on a default alternative.
requirements.original: When considering the compatibility of two union types, initially the first rule (which is not dependent on the existence of a default alternative) shall be applied.

requirements.subject: ent:ttcn3-tool
requirements.canonical: A TTCN-3 tool SHALL use the default-alternative compatibility rules only if the rule based on identically named alternatives has not determined compatibility.
requirements.original: The second rule shall only be used to check compatibility, when - using the first rule - no compatibility has been determined.

ambiguity.issue: 'The second rule' is singular, but the 'Otherwise' bullet contains two default-alternative rules (union-to-arbitrary and arbitrary-to-union). Chose the reading that both are meant.
readings: A TTCN-3 tool SHALL use both default-alternative rules only if the identical-alternative rule has not determined compatibility.
A TTCN-3 tool SHALL use only the union-to-arbitrary default-alternative rule as fallback; the arbitrary-to-union rule applies independently.

requirements.subject: ent:union-type
requirements.canonical: The prescribed order of the union compatibility rules IS intended to avoid ambiguity when a default alternative would also be compatible with the union type itself.
requirements.original: This order shall avoid ambiguity in case that a default alternative would otherwise also be compatible with the union itself.

requirements.subject: ent:union-type
requirements.canonical: A union type with a default alternative CAN be nested within another union type with a default alternative.
requirements.original: NOTE 1: It is possible to have nested unions with default alternatives.

requirements.subject: ent:union-type
requirements.canonical: Type compatibility along default alternatives IS transitive: the outermost union type is compatible with the type of the innermost default alternative if all containing alternatives are default alternatives.
requirements.original: The rules above make type compatibility along the default alternatives transitive, i.e. the outermost union type is compatible with the type of the innermost default union alternative if all containing alternatives are also default alternatives.

requirements.subject: ent:union-value
requirements.canonical: A union value with a default alternative used in an expression IS resolved to its long notation (the default alternative) before the expression is evaluated.
requirements.original: NOTE 2: When a union with a default alternative is used in an expression it will be resolved to its long notation, before the expression is evaluated.

requirements.subject: ent:union-value
requirements.canonical: A union value with a default alternative used directly in a `log` statement IS NOT converted to its default alternative; the union value itself is logged.
requirements.original: log(v_u4);  // results in "{ b:=true }" logged; for backward compatibility when a union value is used in a log statement directly, no conversion is performed.

requirements.subject: ent:anytype
requirements.canonical: An `anytype` type IS NOT compatible with any type other than an `anytype` type.
requirements.original: **anytype types are only compatible with other anytype types.

requirements.subject: ent:anytype
requirements.canonical: An `anytype` value "b" of `anytype` type "B" IS compatible with `anytype` type "A" if the alternative selected in value "b" is also contained in type "A".
requirements.original: An anytype value "b" of anytype type "B" is compatible** with anytype type "A" if the alternative selected in "b" is also contained in "A".

requirements.subject: ent:anytype
requirements.canonical: Only an `anytype` type that is constrained to a fixed set of types via list subtyping CAN cause `anytype` incompatibility, namely when the set of types contained in type "A" does not contain the type selected in value "b".
requirements.original: NOTE: Only anytype types that are constrained to a fixed set of types via list subtyping can be a potential cause for anytype incompatibility, i.e. if the set of types contained in type "A" does not contain the type selected in "b".

requirements.subject: ent:structured-type
requirements.canonical: The structured type compatibility rules of clause 6.3.2 ARE also valid for the sub-structures (fields and elements) of structured types.
requirements.original: The rules defined in this clause for structured types compatibility are also valid for the sub-structure of such types.

requirements.subject: ent:open-type
requirements.canonical: A value of any TTCN-3 type IS compatible with an open type occurring on the left hand side of an assignment.
requirements.original: Values of all existing TTCN-3 types are compatible with the open type occurring in the left hand side of an assignment.

requirements.subject: ent:open-type
requirements.canonical: A value of an open type occurring on the right hand side of an assignment IS compatible with type "A" if the actual value contained in the open type value is compatible with type "A".
requirements.original: Values of open type occurring on the right hand side of an assignment are compatible with a value "a" of a type "A", if the actual value contained in the open type value is compatible with "A".

ambiguity.issue: The rule says the open type value is compatible 'with a value "a" of a type "A"'; compatibility is defined between a value and a type, not between two values.

improper_terms.used: compatible with a value "a" of a type "A"

requirements.subject: ent:component-reference
requirements.condition: a component reference is passed as actual parameter or assigned to a variable of a different component type
requirements.canonical: A component reference "b" of component type "B" IS compatible with component type "A" if all definitions of type "A" have identical definitions in type "B".
requirements.original: 1) Compatibility of a component reference value with a component type (e.g. when passing a component reference as an actual parameter to a function or an altstep or when assigning a component reference value to a variable of different component type): a component reference "b" of component type "B" is compatible with component type "A" if all definitions of "A" have identical definitions in "B".

requirements.subject: ent:function
requirements.canonical: A function or altstep referring to component type "A" in its `runs on` clause MAY be called or started on a component instance of type "B" if all definitions of type "A" have identical definitions in type "B".
requirements.original: 2) Runs on compatibility: a function or altstep referring to component type "A" in its runs on clause may be called or started on a component instance of type 'B' if all the definitions of "A" have identical definitions in "B".

requirements.subject: ent:function
requirements.canonical: A function or altstep referring to component type "A" in its `mtc` clause MAY be called or started in any context that has an `mtc` clause of type "B", or in a testcase with a `runs on` clause of type "B", if all port definitions of type "A" have identical definitions in type "B".
requirements.original: 3) Mtc compatibility: a function or altstep referring to component type "A" in its mtc clause may be called or started in any context that has a mtc clause of type "B" or a testcase with a runs on clause of type "B" if all the port definitions of "A" have identical definitions in "B".

requirements.subject: ent:error
requirements.condition: the type of the MTC is unknown in the calling function
requirements.canonical: If the type of the MTC is unknown in the calling function and component type "A" is not mtc-compatible with the type of the running MTC, a runtime error CAN occur.
requirements.original: If the type of the mtc is unknown in the calling function, this can lead to runtime errors if the component type "A" is not mtc-compatible with the type of the running mtc.

ambiguity.issue: 'can lead to runtime errors' does not say whether a runtime error is mandatory when incompatibility is detected.
readings: A TTCN-3 tool SHALL raise a runtime error when a function with an `mtc` clause of type "A" is called in a context whose running MTC is not mtc-compatible with "A".
A TTCN-3 tool MAY produce a runtime error (or undefined behaviour) in that situation.

requirements.subject: ent:function
requirements.canonical: A function or altstep referring to component type "A" in its `system` clause MAY be called or started in any context that has a `system` clause of type "B", or in a testcase with a `runs on` clause of type "B" and no `system` clause, if all port definitions of type "A" have identical definitions in type "B".
requirements.original: 4) System compatibility: a function or altstep referring to component type "A" in its system clause may be called or started in any context that has a system clause of type "B" or a test case with a runs on clause of type "B" and no system clause if all the port definitions of "A" have identical definitions in "B".

requirements.subject: ent:error
requirements.condition: the type of the system is unknown in the calling function
requirements.canonical: If the type of the system is unknown in the calling function and component type "A" is not system-compatible with the type of the system the current test case was started on, a runtime error CAN occur.
requirements.original: If the type of the system is unknown in the calling function, this can lead to runtime errors if the component type "A" is not system-compatible with the type of the system the current test case was started on.

ambiguity.issue: 'can lead to runtime errors' does not say whether a runtime error is mandatory when incompatibility is detected.
readings: A TTCN-3 tool SHALL raise a runtime error when the system is not system-compatible with "A".
A TTCN-3 tool MAY produce a runtime error in that situation.

requirements.subject: ent:port
requirements.canonical: For component type compatibility, a port instance in type "A" and its counterpart in type "B" SHALL have identical port types and identical identifiers.
requirements.original: a) For port instances, both the type and the identifier shall be identical.

requirements.subject: ent:timer
requirements.canonical: For component type compatibility, a timer instance in type "A" and its counterpart in type "B" SHALL have identical identifiers.
requirements.original: b) For timer instances, identifiers shall be identical and either both shall have identical initial durations or both shall have no initial duration.

requirements.subject: ent:timer
requirements.canonical: For component type compatibility, a timer instance in type "A" and its counterpart in type "B" SHALL either both have identical initial durations or both have no initial duration.
requirements.original: b) For timer instances, identifiers shall be identical and either both shall have identical initial durations or both shall have no initial duration.

requirements.subject: ent:variable
requirements.canonical: For component type compatibility, a variable instance or constant definition in type "A" and its counterpart in type "B" SHALL have identical identifiers and identical types.
requirements.original: c) For variable instances and constant definitions, the identifiers, the types and initialization values shall be identical (in case of variables this means that either the values are missing in both definitions or are the same).

requirements.subject: ent:variable
requirements.canonical: For component type compatibility, a variable instance or constant definition in type "A" and its counterpart in type "B" SHALL have identical initialization values; for variables, either both definitions have no initial value or both have the same value.
requirements.original: c) For variable instances and constant definitions, the identifiers, the types and initialization values shall be identical (in case of variables this means that either the values are missing in both definitions or are the same).

requirements.subject: ent:component-template
requirements.canonical: For component type compatibility, a component template in type "A" and its counterpart in type "B" SHALL have identical identifiers, types, formal parameter lists and assigned template or template field values.
requirements.original: d) For local template definitions, the identifiers, the types, the formal parameter lists and the assigned template or template field values shall be identical.

ambiguity.issue: 'local template definitions' means templates declared in the component type, which the glossary calls component templates.

requirements.subject: ent:communication-operation
requirements.canonical: The communication operations `send`, `receive`, `trigger`, `call`, `getcall`, `reply`, `getreply` and `raise` SHALL apply strong typing instead of type compatibility.
requirements.original: The communication operations (see clause 22) `send, receive, trigger, call, getcall, reply, getreply` and raise and connection operations connect, map, disconnect and unmap (see clause 21.1) are exceptions to the weaker rule of type compatibility and require strong typing.

ambiguity.issue: The list omits `catch` (and `check`), while 6.3.4-s003/s004 treat `catch` like `raise`. Chose the literal list.
readings: Only the listed operations `send`, `receive`, `trigger`, `call`, `getcall`, `reply`, `getreply` and `raise` SHALL apply strong typing.
All communication operations of clause 22, including `catch` and `check`, SHALL apply strong typing.

requirements.subject: ent:connection-operation
requirements.canonical: The connection operations `connect`, `map`, `disconnect` and `unmap` SHALL apply strong typing instead of type compatibility.
requirements.original: The communication operations (see clause 22) `send, receive, trigger, call, getcall, reply, getreply` and raise and connection operations connect, map, disconnect and unmap (see clause 21.1) are exceptions to the weaker rule of type compatibility and require strong typing.

requirements.subject: ent:port-type
requirements.canonical: The type of a value or template used directly as argument of a `send`, `receive` or `trigger` operation SHALL be explicitly listed in the definition of the port type of the port the operation is applied to.
requirements.original: The types of values or templates directly used as parameters of the operations send, receive and trigger shall also be explicitly defined in the associated port type definition.

requirements.subject: ent:signature
requirements.canonical: The signature of the parameter list given to a `call`, `getcall`, `reply` or `getreply` operation, and the signature given to a `catch` or `raise` operation, SHALL be explicitly listed in the definition of the port type of the port the operation is applied to.
requirements.original: The signature type of the parameter list given to the operations call, getcall, reply, getreply and the signature type given to the operations catch and raise shall also be explicitly defined in the associated port type definition.

requirements.subject: ent:exception
requirements.canonical: The type of a value or template used directly as exception in a `catch` or `raise` operation SHALL be explicitly listed in the exception list of the signature given to the operation.
requirements.original: The types of values or templates directly used as exceptions to the operations catch and raise shall be explicitly defined in the exceptions part of the definition of the signature given to the operation.

requirements.subject: ent:receive-operation
requirements.canonical: A `receive` operation whose template is of a type "T" SHALL NOT match a message that was sent as a value or template of a different type, even if that type is a synonym of type "T".
requirements.original: p.receive (MyRec:?); // shall not match as the transmitted template is of the alias type and not of the user-defined type

requirements.subject: ent:value-redirect
requirements.canonical: Storing the value of a received message in a variable by a value redirect IS NOT subject to strong typing; the variable needs only be of a compatible type.
requirements.original: var MyRec v_x; p.receive (MyRecAlias:?) -> value v_x; // shall not cause an error since storing the value requires no strong typing

requirements.subject: ent:value
requirements.condition: the source and target types have different root types
requirements.canonical: When a value has to be converted to a type with a different root type, the conversion SHALL use one of the predefined conversion functions of clause 16.1.2 or a user-defined function.
requirements.original: If it is necessary to convert values of one type to values of another type, because their types have different root types, then either one of the predefined conversion functions defined in clause 16.1.2 or a user defined function shall be used.

requirements.subject: ent:port
